appellations.name: Scharzhofberg
appellations.summary: The Scharzhofberg is the Saar's crown and, for many, the purest expression of German Riesling anywhere. A single south-facing whale-back of grey Devonian slate rising above the Scharzhof manor between Wiltingen and Oberemmel, it gives wines of glassy acidity, almost weightless body and a perfume of white peach, citrus peel and wet stone that can take decades to unfold. Egon Müller's sweet Kabinett, Spätlese and Auslese set the benchmark, and his Trockenbeerenauslesen are among the most expensive wines ever auctioned: a 2003 TBA fetched 14,566 euros a bottle at the VDP Mosel auction in 2015. Van Volxem, Reichsgraf von Kesselstatt, Vereinigte Hospitien and the Bischöfliche Weingüter also own parcels.
appellations.terroir: About 28 ha of vines on a steep, open slope from the valley floor to the wooded crest. Thin, stony grey slate warms quickly, but the Saar valley is cooler and windier than the Middle Mosel, so ripening is slow and late: in lean years the wines are taut, in warm years they gain an incomparable tension between ripeness and acidity.
appellations.nerd_note: Legally the Scharzhofberg is an Ortsteil (a named part of Wiltingen), which is why its wines carry no village prefix and why the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register files its 28 ha as 'Einzellagenfrei'. On Clotten's 1868 Prussian tax map it is shaded dark red, the top class.

appellations.name: Wiltingener Braune Kupp
appellations.summary: A small, steep amphitheatre of brown-weathering slate just upstream of Wiltingen, the Braune Kupp is the monopole of Weingut Le Gallais, which Egon Müller's family has run since 1954. The wines are a shade broader and spicier than the neighbouring Scharzhofberg, with ripe yellow fruit, a smoky note and the same razor-sharp Saar acidity. Müller bottles them separately under the Le Gallais label, mostly as fruity-sweet Kabinett, Spätlese and Auslese that age as long as their more famous siblings.
appellations.terroir: Iron-tinged Devonian slate on a south-facing curve that traps warmth; the bowl shape gives it a slightly earlier ripening rhythm than the open Scharzhofberg. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Saar and the Grosslage Scharzberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages). Neighbouring sites in Wiltingen include Klosterberg, Braunfels, Kupp and Gottesfuß.
appellations.nerd_note: The name means 'brown dome', after the colour of the weathered rock rather than any wine style.

appellations.name: Wiltingener Gottesfuß
appellations.summary: Gottesfuß ('God's foot') is a tiny, very steep slope at the edge of Wiltingen that Van Volxem has made famous with ungrafted vines planted more than a century ago. The site gives dense, chiselled dry Riesling with a herbal, almost saline finish and the concentration that only old, low-yielding vines provide. Around 3.5 ha are registered under vine.
appellations.terroir: Grey and blue Devonian slate with little topsoil on a sheltered south-facing flank; the old own-rooted vines dig deep into the fissured rock. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Saar and the Grosslage Scharzberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 3.5 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Wiltingen include Klosterberg, Braunfels, Braune Kupp and Kupp.
appellations.nerd_note: Phylloxera never took hold in much of the Saar's slate, which is why parcels like this still carry pre-1900 ungrafted vines.

appellations.name: Wiltingener Kupp
appellations.summary: The Wiltinger Kupp is a compact, south-east-facing hill above the village, worked mainly by Van Volxem and the Bischöfliche Weingüter. Its Rieslings are firm and mineral with a cooler, more citric profile than the Braune Kupp next door.
appellations.terroir: Grey slate on a convex slope that catches morning sun and the cooling Saar breeze. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Saar and the Grosslage Scharzberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 7 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Wiltingen include Klosterberg, Braunfels, Braune Kupp and Gottesfuß.

appellations.name: Wiltingener Braunfels
appellations.summary: A larger Wiltingen site (about 20 ha) on the road towards Kanzem, Braunfels is a source of elegant, mid-weight Saar Riesling from growers such as Van Volxem and Jordan & Jordan. It sits a step below the village's grand sites but shows the same slate-driven tension.
appellations.terroir: Slate with more weathered loam on gentler pitches; ripens a little later than the steep core of Wiltingen. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Saar and the Grosslage Scharzberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 20.4 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Wiltingen include Klosterberg, Braune Kupp, Kupp and Gottesfuß.

appellations.name: Wiltingener Klosterberg
appellations.summary: Wiltingen's largest Einzellage (about 50 ha), the Klosterberg spreads over the hills behind the village. It gives fresh, slatey Riesling of varying ambition; the best parcels show that much of the old Saar fame lay in small named plots that the 1971 law folded into larger Einzellagen.
appellations.terroir: Mixed grey slate and loam, from steep to rolling; quality depends heavily on the parcel. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Saar and the Grosslage Scharzberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 49.9 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Wiltingen include Braunfels, Braune Kupp, Kupp and Gottesfuß.

appellations.name: Wiltingener Hölle
appellations.summary: Hölle ('hell') is a very small, hot pocket of steep slate in Wiltingen whose name reflects the heat that builds up in summer. It yields concentrated, ripe Saar Riesling from a handful of growers.
appellations.terroir: South-facing slate bowl, sheltered from wind. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Saar and the Grosslage Scharzberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages). Neighbouring sites in Wiltingen include Klosterberg, Braunfels, Braune Kupp and Kupp.

appellations.name: Altenberg
appellations.summary: The Kanzemer Altenberg is one of the steepest and most dramatic slopes on the Saar, a wall of slate rising directly from the river opposite Kanzem. Von Othegraven, owned since 2010 by the television presenter Günther Jauch, whose family has roots in the estate, is the reference grower; Van Volxem and the Bischöfliche Weingüter also bottle it. The wines are powerful by Saar standards, with yellow fruit, smoke and a long stony finish, and the dry Grosses Gewächs ages superbly.
appellations.terroir: Around 19 ha of grey and blue slate with weathered diabase, pitched up to about 70 percent and facing south-south-west straight over the water, which reflects light and moderates frost. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Saar and the Grosslage Scharzberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 19.1 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Filzen include Pulchen.
appellations.nerd_note: Clotten's 1868 tax map did not list the Altenberg among the top Saar sites; its fame grew later, as Lars Carlberg's study of the map points out.

appellations.name: Kanzemer Sonnenberg
appellations.summary: Kanzem's broad Sonnenberg (about 20 ha) runs along the right bank of the Saar and gives lighter, fragrant Riesling, often made fruity-sweet in the Kabinett style.
appellations.terroir: Slate and loam on moderately steep south-west slopes. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Saar and the Grosslage Scharzberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 19.9 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Kanzem include Hörecker.

appellations.name: Kanzemer Hörecker
appellations.summary: A tiny, historic Kanzem site, the Hörecker was once among the most expensive vineyards of the Saar and is today a rarity bottled by only a few estates.
appellations.terroir: Steep slate pocket close to the Altenberg. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Saar and the Grosslage Scharzberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages). Neighbouring sites in Kanzem include Sonnenberg.

appellations.name: Kupp
appellations.summary: The Ayler Kupp is a broad, steep slope of slate above Ayl, about 50 ha in its modern form. Peter Lauer turned it into one of the Saar's most studied sites by bottling historic parcels separately under cask numbers: Kern, Stirn, Unterstenberg and Schonfels each show a different face, from delicate and floral to dense and smoky. The Bischöfliche Weingüter and several smaller growers also work here. The best wines combine Saar acidity with a creamy texture that comes from old vines and long lees ageing.
appellations.terroir: Grey and blue Devonian slate with patches of weathered rock and loam, south to south-east facing, roughly 150 to 300 m; the side valley of the Ayl brook brings cool night air. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Saar and the Grosslage Scharzberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 53.3 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Ayl include Herrenberger.
appellations.nerd_note: Lauer's parcel names come from the old cadastre, many of them erased when the 1971 wine law merged small sites into larger Einzellagen.

appellations.name: Ayler Herrenberger
appellations.summary: A small Ayl site long associated with the Bischöfliches Konvikt of Trier, the Herrenberger gives lean, floral Saar Riesling.
appellations.terroir: Steep slate on a south-facing spur. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Saar and the Grosslage Scharzberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages). Neighbouring sites in Ayl include Kupp.

appellations.name: Ockfener Bockstein
appellations.summary: The Bockstein is Ockfen's great slope, about 52 ha of slate rising high above a side valley of the Saar. It is cooler and later-ripening than the Scharzhofberg, and its Rieslings are classically racy with grapefruit, herbs and a cool slate finish; in warm vintages it shines with fruity-sweet Kabinett and Spätlese. Sankt Urbans-Hof, Dr. Fischer, Zilliken and Van Volxem are among the owners.
appellations.terroir: Grey Devonian slate on a steep, south and south-west-facing slope from roughly 170 to 350 m, exposed to wind from the Hunsrück; the height of the slope keeps acidity high. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Saar and the Grosslage Scharzberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 51.7 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Ockfen include Geisberg.
appellations.nerd_note: Ockfen sits a little away from the Saar itself, so the Bockstein gets less of the river's warming effect than sites that rise straight out of the water.

appellations.name: Geisberg
appellations.summary: The Geisberg rises above Ockfen and Schoden to over 400 m, one of the highest sites on the Saar. Long abandoned, it has been cleared and replanted by Van Volxem, whose dry Geisberg Riesling is cool, perfumed and taut.
appellations.terroir: High, steep slate with a strong wind exposure; only a few hectares are under vine. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Saar and the Grosslage Scharzberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 3.5 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Ockfen include Bockstein.
appellations.nerd_note: Van Volxem's Roman Niewodniczanski replanted the Geisberg after studying the old Prussian maps and price lists that ranked Saar sites a century and more ago.

appellations.name: Saarburger Rausch
appellations.summary: The Saarburger Rausch is the signature site of Forstmeister Geltz Zilliken, a steep slope of slate above Saarburg laced with a volcanic diabase intrusion. Zilliken's fruity-sweet Kabinett, Spätlese and Auslese from the Rausch are some of the most age-worthy wines of the Mosel, with a smoky, spicy note and a nervy acidity that keeps them fresh for decades. The estate's cellar, dug three storeys deep, keeps temperatures low and fermentations slow.
appellations.terroir: Around 18 ha of grey slate mixed with greenish diabase (greenstone), south-facing at roughly 200 to 300 m; the hard diabase holds less water and stresses the vines. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Saar and the Grosslage Scharzberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 18.5 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Saarburg include Kupp.
appellations.nerd_note: The diabase gives the Rausch a smoky, spicy signature that tasters pick out even in very young wines.

appellations.name: Saarburger Kupp
appellations.summary: A Saarburg slope above the town, the Kupp gives light, floral Riesling for several local estates.
appellations.terroir: Slate on a south-east-facing hill. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Saar and the Grosslage Scharzberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 10.6 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Saarburg include Rausch.

appellations.name: Serriger Schloß Saarsteiner
appellations.summary: The monopole of Schloss Saarstein, a villa-estate high above the Saar near Serrig, this is one of the coolest sites of the valley. The Ebert family makes bright, piercing Riesling and elegant Pinot Blanc here.
appellations.terroir: Steep slate on a south-facing bend of the river, among the most upstream top sites of the Saar. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Saar and the Grosslage Scharzberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages). Neighbouring sites in Serrig include Herrenberg, Schloß Saarfelser Schloßberg and Würtzberg.

appellations.name: Serriger Herrenberg
appellations.summary: Serrig's Herrenberg is a cool, late-ripening slope that gives tart, stony Riesling in lean years and thrilling ones in warm vintages. Serrig was a centre of Prussian state viticulture.
appellations.terroir: Slate on steep south-west slopes near the upper limit of the Saar vineyards. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Saar and the Grosslage Scharzberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages). Neighbouring sites in Serrig include Schloß Saarfelser Schloßberg, Schloß Saarsteiner and Würtzberg.

appellations.name: Serriger Würtzberg
appellations.summary: The Würtzberg in Serrig, about 5.5 ha registered, gives lean, aromatic Riesling and lent its name to an estate founded on Prussian-era vineyards.
appellations.terroir: Steep slate on the Saar's cool upper reaches. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Saar and the Grosslage Scharzberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 5.5 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Serrig include Herrenberg, Schloß Saarfelser Schloßberg and Schloß Saarsteiner.

appellations.name: Serriger Schloß Saarfelser Schloßberg
appellations.summary: A Serrig site named after the Saarfels castle-estate, giving cool, crisp Riesling from steep slate.
appellations.terroir: Slate slopes on the upstream Saar. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Saar and the Grosslage Scharzberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages). Neighbouring sites in Serrig include Herrenberg, Schloß Saarsteiner and Würtzberg.

appellations.name: Oberemmeler Hütte
appellations.summary: The Hütte is the small, walled monopole of Weingut von Hövel in Oberemmel, a former property of St. Maximin abbey in Trier. It gives delicate, finely etched Riesling with a floral lift.
appellations.terroir: Steep slate on a south-facing side-valley slope. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Saar and the Grosslage Scharzberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages). Neighbouring sites in Oberemmel include Rosenberg and Agritiusberg.

appellations.name: Oberemmeler Agritiusberg
appellations.summary: A small Oberemmel site named after St. Agritius, a fourth-century bishop of Trier, once more highly regarded than it is today.
appellations.terroir: Slate on the Oberemmel side valley. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Saar and the Grosslage Scharzberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 2.7 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Oberemmel include Rosenberg and Hütte.

appellations.name: Oberemmeler Rosenberg
appellations.summary: Oberemmel's largest site (about 35 ha), the Rosenberg gives medium-bodied, floral Saar Riesling, notably from Reichsgraf von Kesselstatt.
appellations.terroir: Slate and loam in the Oberemmel valley, cooler than the main Saar. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Saar and the Grosslage Scharzberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 34.9 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Oberemmel include Agritiusberg and Hütte.

appellations.name: Wawerner Goldberg
appellations.summary: The Wawerner Goldberg is a south-facing amphitheatre in a little side valley of the Saar that had fallen out of use before Van Volxem bought and replanted it. The site is now a VDP.GROSSE LAGE and gives full, golden-fruited dry Riesling with Saar spine.
appellations.terroir: About 12 ha of slate in a warm, wind-protected bowl. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Saar and the Grosslage Scharzberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 12 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Wawern include Herrenberger.

appellations.name: Wawerner Herrenberger
appellations.summary: A small Wawern site with a long reputation for fine, fragrant Riesling, bottled by a few estates including Dr. Fischer.
appellations.terroir: Slate on a steep south-facing slope. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Saar and the Grosslage Scharzberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 3.6 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Wawern include Goldberg.

appellations.name: Filzener Pulchen
appellations.summary: A small, steep site in Filzen, the Pulchen is the home vineyard of Weingut Piedmont and gives fine, lively Saar Riesling.
appellations.terroir: Slate on a south-east-facing slope above the lower Saar. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Saar and the Grosslage Scharzberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 2.3 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Filzen include Altenberg.

appellations.name: Schodener Saarfeilser Marienberg
appellations.summary: A tiny Schoden site with a historic double name, giving taut, cool Saar Riesling.
appellations.terroir: Steep slate on the Saar's left bank. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Saar and the Grosslage Scharzberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 3.4 ha are registered under vine.

appellations.name: Mertesdorfer Abtsberg
appellations.summary: The Abtsberg is the jewel of Maximin Grünhaus, the walled estate at the foot of a steep slope in the Ruwer valley that Emperor Otto I gave to St. Maximin abbey of Trier in 966. Monks worked it until Napoleon's secularisation; the von Schubert family has owned it since 1882. Abtsberg Rieslings are delicate and intensely mineral, with blackcurrant leaf, citrus and a lingering blue-slate finish, magnificent both dry and fruity-sweet.
appellations.terroir: Blue Devonian slate on a south to south-east-facing slope up to about 70 percent, in a narrow, cool side valley where Rieslings ripen late and keep high acidity. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Ruwer and belongs to no Grosslage. Neighbouring sites in Mertesdorf include Herrenberg and Bruderberg.
appellations.nerd_note: On Clotten's 1868 map the Abtsberg was shaded dark red but labelled Herrenberg; the estate's three sites (Abtsberg, Herrenberg, Bruderberg) were once allocated to the abbot, the monastery and the brothers.

appellations.name: Mertesdorfer Herrenberg
appellations.summary: The second great site of Maximin Grünhaus, the Herrenberg lies just downstream of the Abtsberg on red-tinged slate. Its wines are broader and fruitier, with ripe apricot and spice, and the estate also grows Pinot Noir here. The von Schubert family still runs the estate; the Herrenberg's Kabinett is often the most approachable of the three Grünhaus sites when young, while its Auslesen turn honeyed and spicy over twenty years.
appellations.terroir: About 28 ha (registered vine area) of red and grey slate with more iron, slightly warmer than the Abtsberg. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Ruwer and belongs to no Grosslage; about 28.2 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Mertesdorf include Abtsberg and Bruderberg.
appellations.nerd_note: In monastic times the Herrenberg's wine went to the 'Herren', the monks of St. Maximin.

appellations.name: Mertesdorfer Bruderberg
appellations.summary: The smallest of Maximin Grünhaus's three sites, the Bruderberg was historically the lay brothers' vineyard. It gives a firm, spicy Riesling bottled in small quantities.
appellations.terroir: Iron-rich slate on a steep, south-facing slope at the downstream end of the Grünhaus hill. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Ruwer and belongs to no Grosslage. Neighbouring sites in Mertesdorf include Herrenberg and Abtsberg.

appellations.name: Eitelsbacher Karthäuserhofberg
appellations.summary: The Karthäuserhofberg is the monopole of the Karthäuserhof in Eitelsbach, an estate that belonged to the Carthusians of Trier from 1335 until Napoleon's secularisation, when it was auctioned in 1811 to Valentin Leonardy, whose descendants, the Rautenstrauch and Tyrell families, ran it for two centuries. The wines are among the Ruwer's most aristocratic: fine-boned, smoky and very long, with acidity that carries them for decades. The estate is known for its neck-only label, a nineteenth-century design that leaves the bottle body bare.
appellations.terroir: About 19 ha of grey and red Devonian slate on a south-facing slope rising behind the manor, cool and windy in the narrow Ruwer valley. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Ruwer and belongs to no Grosslage.
appellations.nerd_note: Every wine the estate makes comes from this one slope, so the Karthäuserhofberg is as much a brand as a vineyard.

appellations.name: Kaseler Nies'chen
appellations.summary: The Nies'chen is Kasel's finest slope, a steep amphitheatre of blue slate whose Rieslings are perfumed, delicate and chalky-fine. Reichsgraf von Kesselstatt, Erben von Beulwitz and the Bischöfliche Weingüter all make benchmark fruity-sweet and dry wines here. The Ruwer is so narrow and cool that its Rieslings are often the lightest of the whole Mosel, with Kabinetts of 7.5 to 8.5 percent alcohol quite normal, and the Nies'chen's blue slate adds a floral, almost violet lift.
appellations.terroir: About 14 ha of blue Devonian slate on a south-west-facing slope in the cool Ruwer valley. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Ruwer and belongs to no Grosslage; about 14.1 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Kasel include Hitzlay and Kehrnagel.

appellations.name: Kaseler Kehrnagel
appellations.summary: A steep Kasel site of about 11 ha, the Kehrnagel gives racy, citrus-scented Riesling, notably for Reichsgraf von Kesselstatt.
appellations.terroir: Grey slate on a south-facing slope. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Ruwer and belongs to no Grosslage; about 10.7 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Kasel include Hitzlay and Nies'chen.

appellations.name: Kaseler Hitzlay
appellations.summary: Kasel's Hitzlay ('heat rock') is a warm pocket of slate giving riper, more aromatic Ruwer Riesling than its cooler neighbours.
appellations.terroir: Slate outcrop that reflects and stores heat. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Ruwer and belongs to no Grosslage; about 8.3 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Kasel include Kehrnagel and Nies'chen.

appellations.name: Kürenzer Altenberg
appellations.summary: A Trier site on the slopes of Kürenz and Avelsbach, near the vineyards the Prussian state domain developed in the late nineteenth century. It gives fine, cool Riesling within sight of the city.
appellations.terroir: Slate slopes at the mouth of the Ruwer and Avelsbach valleys. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Römerlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages).

appellations.name: Trittenheimer Apotheke
appellations.summary: The Apotheke is a long, steep wall of slate across the river from Trittenheim, about 65 ha that run around a bend of the Mosel. Grans-Fassian, Ansgar Clüsserath and Josef Milz are its best-known growers, and it produces some of the most finely balanced dry Rieslings of the Middle Mosel: peach and citrus, a smoky slate edge and a lively finish. Old ungrafted vines survive in several parcels.
appellations.terroir: Grey and blue Devonian slate on slopes up to 70 percent, mostly south-west facing, from the river at about 120 m up to roughly 300 m; the broad water surface reflects light and tempers frost. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Michelsberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 65.1 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Trittenheim include Altärchen, Felsenkopf and Leiterchen.
appellations.nerd_note: Workers once had to cross the river by ferry to reach the slope; the modern bridge only came in the twentieth century.

appellations.name: Trittenheimer Altärchen
appellations.summary: Trittenheim's big Altärchen (about 155 ha) wraps around the village side of the river bend and is a source of honest, fruity Riesling, with a few steep parcels capable of much more.
appellations.terroir: Slate and weathered loam, from steep to gentle. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Michelsberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 154.9 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Trittenheim include Apotheke, Felsenkopf and Leiterchen.

appellations.name: Trittenheimer Felsenkopf
appellations.summary: The Felsenkopf ('rock head') is a tiny, very steep outcrop above Trittenheim owned by Josef Milz, who makes a concentrated, mineral Riesling here. It is classified as a VDP.GROSSE LAGE.
appellations.terroir: Bare slate rock with almost no topsoil. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Michelsberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages). Neighbouring sites in Trittenheim include Altärchen, Apotheke and Leiterchen.

appellations.name: Trittenheimer Leiterchen
appellations.summary: The Leiterchen ('little ladder') is a narrow strip of steep slate in Trittenheim, a monopole of Josef Milz. Its Riesling is fine and floral, and the site is a VDP.GROSSE LAGE.
appellations.terroir: Steep slate so narrow that workers once climbed it by ladder. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Michelsberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages). Neighbouring sites in Trittenheim include Altärchen, Apotheke and Felsenkopf.

appellations.name: Leiwener Laurentiuslay
appellations.summary: The Laurentiuslay is Leiwen's great slope, crowned by a small chapel of St. Lawrence on a rocky ridge across the river from the village. Grans-Fassian, Carl Loewen and Sankt Urbans-Hof make powerful, spicy dry Rieslings and luscious Auslesen here; the site's old vines give density without heaviness.
appellations.terroir: About 16 ha of grey and blue slate with quartzite, very steep, facing south and south-west over the Mosel. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Sankt Michael (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 16.1 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Leiwen include Klostergarten.
appellations.nerd_note: Leiwen was known for volume production on the flats after the 1970s land consolidations; the Laurentiuslay helped growers like Gerhard Grans prove the village's steep slopes could rank with the best.

appellations.name: Leiwener Klostergarten
appellations.summary: A large, flatter Leiwen site of about 240 ha giving everyday Riesling and Müller-Thurgau; Carl Loewen makes a fine old-vine wine from a better parcel.
appellations.terroir: Gravel and loam on the inside of the river bend. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Sankt Michael (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 240.3 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Leiwen include Laurentiuslay.

appellations.name: Klöerather Bruderschaft
appellations.summary: Klüsserath's Bruderschaft is a long, steep slope of about 186 ha, revived by growers such as Kirsten and Friedrich-Wilhelm-Gymnasium, giving bright, mineral Riesling.
appellations.terroir: Slate on a south-facing curve of the river. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Sankt Michael (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 186.2 ha are registered under vine.

appellations.name: Thörnicher Ritsch
appellations.summary: The Ritsch is a steep slope above Thörnich that Carl Loewen helped rescue from abandonment. Its Riesling is cool, smoky and tightly wound.
appellations.terroir: About 15 ha of slate on a south-west-facing slope at a narrow part of the valley. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Sankt Michael (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 15.1 ha are registered under vine.

appellations.name: Longuicher Maximiner Herrenberg
appellations.summary: This Longuich site was once owned by St. Maximin abbey in Trier. Carl Loewen holds a parcel of ungrafted Riesling planted in 1896, among the oldest productive vineyards in Germany, and bottles it as '1896'.
appellations.terroir: About 12 ha of red slate and weathered sandstone on a south-facing slope. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Probstberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 12.2 ha are registered under vine.
appellations.nerd_note: The 1896 vines were planted at a time when Riesling cuttings were still propagated by massal selection from the slope itself.

appellations.name: Goldtröpfchen
appellations.summary: Piesport's Goldtröpfchen is one of the Mosel's most perfect natural amphitheatres, a south-facing bowl curving around the village that gives some of the most opulent, aromatic Rieslings of the valley: blackcurrant, peach, citrus and a hint of spice over a juicy slate core. Reinhold Haart, Julian Haart, Reichsgraf von Kesselstatt, Sankt Urbans-Hof and Grans-Fassian are the names to look for. The site's reputation was blurred for decades by the bulk wine 'Piesporter Michelsberg', a Grosslage that borrowed the village's fame.
appellations.terroir: Grey Devonian slate with a deeper, more fertile weathered layer on a steep south-facing bowl; the Mosel bends around it so that heat and light are reflected back onto the vines. The 2026 vineyard register lists about 64 ha under vine across Piesport, Niederemmel and Dhron. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Michelsberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 64.5 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Dhron include Hofberger, Roterd and Häs'chen.
appellations.nerd_note: Archaeologists found a Roman wine press house in Piesport in 1985, one of the largest north of the Alps, a sign that this bowl has been prized for at least 1,600 years.

appellations.name: Piesporter Domherr
appellations.summary: The Domherr ('cathedral canon') is a small, steep heart of the Piesport amphitheatre, historically owned by the Trier cathedral chapter. Its Riesling is concentrated and finely spiced.
appellations.terroir: About 4 ha of slate in the steepest part of the bowl. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Michelsberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 4.2 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Piesport include Schubertslay.

appellations.name: Piesporter Schubertslay
appellations.summary: A tiny, very steep rock face in Piesport that Julian Haart and a few others have revived, giving intense, stony Riesling.
appellations.terroir: Bare slate cliff facing south. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Michelsberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages). Neighbouring sites in Piesport include Domherr.

appellations.name: Hofberger
appellations.summary: The Hofberger rises above the Dhron valley where the little river joins the Mosel. Andreas Adam of A.J. Adam has made it famous again with taut, smoky Rieslings, including from very old vines. Its cooler side-valley exposure gives a precise, almost Saar-like acidity.
appellations.terroir: Grey slate on steep south and south-west slopes in the mouth of the Dhron valley, cooled by air draining down the side valley; about 73 ha are registered under vine. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Michelsberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 73.1 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Dhron include Roterd, Goldtröpfchen and Häs'chen.
appellations.nerd_note: A 'Dhronhofberger' features in the VDP Mosel's early auction history, a sign of its standing a century ago.

appellations.name: Dhroner Roterd
appellations.summary: The Roterd ('red earth') above Dhron owes its name to red, iron-rich weathered slate. It gives warm, aromatic Riesling.
appellations.terroir: Red slate soils on a south-facing slope of the Dhron valley. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Michelsberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 44.2 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Dhron include Hofberger, Goldtröpfchen and Häs'chen.

appellations.name: Dhroner Häs'chen
appellations.summary: A tiny, steep parcel in Dhron that A.J. Adam bottles separately, giving fine, floral Riesling.
appellations.terroir: Slate on a sheltered slope in the Dhron valley. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Michelsberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages). Neighbouring sites in Dhron include Hofberger, Roterd and Goldtröpfchen.

appellations.name: Neumagener Rosengärtchen
appellations.summary: A Neumagen site of about 23 ha, close to the place where the stone relief of a Roman wine ship was found in 1878. It gives lively, medium-weight Riesling.
appellations.terroir: Slate and loam on south-facing slopes. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Michelsberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 22.8 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Neumagen include Laudamusberg.

appellations.name: Neumagener Laudamusberg
appellations.summary: A steep Neumagen slope of about 22 ha, giving firm, slatey Riesling.
appellations.terroir: Grey slate on the left bank. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Michelsberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 22.3 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Neumagen include Rosengärtchen.

appellations.name: Wintricher Ohligsberg
appellations.summary: The Ohligsberg is a very steep, rock-strewn slope above Wintrich, owned almost entirely by Reinhold Haart. Its Riesling is dense and mineral, with a distinctive smoky, almost flinty character. The slope is so stony that machines are useless here; vines are trained on single stakes (Einzelpfahl), the traditional Mosel system, and every task is done by hand.
appellations.terroir: About 7 ha of bare blue and grey slate, among the steepest sites of the Middle Mosel. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Kurfürstlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 6.9 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Wintrich include Großer Herrgott.
appellations.nerd_note: In the nineteenth century the Ohligsberg's wines were sold at prices to rival the best of Piesport.

appellations.name: Wintricher Großer Herrgott
appellations.summary: A large Wintrich site of about 90 ha named after a wayside crucifix, giving fruity, accessible Riesling.
appellations.terroir: Slate and loam on moderate slopes. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Kurfürstlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 90.8 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Wintrich include Ohligsberg.

appellations.name: Kestener Paulinshofberger
appellations.summary: A Kesten site of about 18 ha named after the Paulinshof, a former property of St. Paulinus in Trier. Weingut Paulinshof and Fritz Haag make fine Riesling here.
appellations.terroir: Slate on a south-facing slope opposite the Brauneberg. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Kurfürstlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 17.9 ha are registered under vine.

appellations.name: Juffer
appellations.summary: The Juffer is the broad, steep wall of slate opposite Brauneberg, the village that was called Dusemond (from mons dulcis, 'sweet hill') until 1925. Its Rieslings are rich, ripe and spicy, with a juicy core and a long slate finish. Fritz Haag, Schloss Lieser, Max Ferd. Richter, Paulinshof and Willi Haag are the key growers.
appellations.terroir: Grey Devonian slate with weathered loam on a south-south-east-facing slope rising from the river; the Mosel is wide here and reflects a lot of light. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Kurfürstlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 31.8 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Brauneberg include Juffer Sonnenuhr and Kammer.
appellations.nerd_note: Local lore says the name comes from 'Jungfer' (young lady), after unmarried daughters of a local official who owned parcels here.

appellations.name: Brauneberger Juffer Sonnenuhr
appellations.summary: The Juffer-Sonnenuhr is the steep core of the Brauneberger Juffer, marked by a sundial. In the hands of Fritz Haag (and of Schloss Lieser, run by Thomas Haag) it yields some of the most complete Rieslings of the Mosel: creamy, concentrated, layered with peach, spice and slate, and capable of ageing for decades. Nineteenth-century price lists already placed Brauneberg among the first villages of the Mosel.
appellations.terroir: About 10.6 ha of grey slate on the steepest, best-exposed part of the slope, facing south directly over the river. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Kurfürstlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 10.6 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Brauneberg include Juffer and Kammer.
appellations.nerd_note: Fritz Haag's Auslese gold capsules and long-gold capsules from the Juffer-Sonnenuhr are among the most collected sweet Rieslings in the world.

appellations.name: Brauneberger Kammer
appellations.summary: A small, walled Brauneberg site long associated with Weingut Paulinshof, giving ripe, fine-textured Riesling.
appellations.terroir: Slate in a sheltered position next to the Juffer. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Kurfürstlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages). Neighbouring sites in Brauneberg include Juffer and Juffer Sonnenuhr.

appellations.name: Lieserer Niederberg-Helden
appellations.summary: The Niederberg-Helden is a steep south-facing slope above Lieser that Thomas Haag of Schloss Lieser has restored to prominence. Its Riesling is spicy and powerful, with a cool blue-slate thread. Schloss Lieser, the neo-Gothic manor in the village, was revived after Thomas Haag, son of Wilhelm Haag of Fritz Haag, took over as winemaker in 1992; his family later bought the estate. The 1971 law joined the historic Niederberg and Helden slopes into one Einzellage.
appellations.terroir: About 30 ha of blue and grey slate on a steep slope at the mouth of the Lieser valley. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Kurfürstlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 29.9 ha are registered under vine.

appellations.name: Mülheimer Helenenkloster
appellations.summary: A small monopole of Max Ferd. Richter in Mülheim, the Helenenkloster is famous for Eiswein, which the estate has made here in many years.
appellations.terroir: A cool site where early frosts let the estate freeze grapes on the vine in many winters. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Kurfürstlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages).

appellations.name: Bernkasteler Doctor
appellations.summary: The Doctor is Germany's most famous vineyard, a tiny, very steep slope rising directly behind the rooftops of Bernkastel. Legend says its wine cured the fourteenth-century Archbishop Boemund II of Trier of a fever. In 1900 a small parcel is said to have sold for 100 gold marks per vine, a record price for vineyard land. Wwe. Dr. H. Thanisch (both branches), Wegeler and Lauerburg share it, and the wines are rich, smoky and long, with a distinctive mineral warmth.
appellations.terroir: About 3.3 ha of weathered grey slate on a south-south-west slope of up to 60 percent, sheltered by the town and the Kueser Plateau; it ripens early and gets very warm. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Münzlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 3.3 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Bernkastel include Badstube, Graben, Lay and Alte Badstube am Doctorberg.
appellations.nerd_note: When the 1971 wine law tried to enlarge the Doctor to take in neighbouring slopes, the owners went to court; the boundary finally settled at about 3.3 ha, still a fraction of its neighbours.

appellations.name: Bernkasteler Alte Badstube am Doctorberg
appellations.summary: A tiny slope next to the Doctor, the Alte Badstube am Doctorberg gives very similar, rich and smoky Riesling at a fraction of the price.
appellations.terroir: About 1.6 ha of slate on the same steep hillside as the Doctor. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Münzlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 1.6 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Bernkastel include Badstube, Graben, Lay and Doctor.

appellations.name: Bernkasteler Lay
appellations.summary: The Lay is a steep slope just downstream of the Doctor, overlooking the bridge at Bernkastel. Its Rieslings are fine and elegant, with a cooler profile than its famous neighbour.
appellations.terroir: About 9.5 ha of grey slate ('Lay' means slate rock) facing south-west. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Münzlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 9.5 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Bernkastel include Badstube, Graben, Alte Badstube am Doctorberg and Doctor.

appellations.name: Bernkasteler Graben
appellations.summary: A steep Bernkastel slope of about 10 ha next to the Doctor, giving spicy, concentrated Riesling.
appellations.terroir: Slate on a south-facing slope above the town. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Münzlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 10.3 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Bernkastel include Badstube, Lay, Alte Badstube am Doctorberg and Doctor.

appellations.name: Bernkasteler Badstube
appellations.summary: Badstube is a collective Einzellage name for several steep Bernkastel slopes around the Doctor, about 26 ha, giving fruity, accessible Riesling.
appellations.terroir: Slate slopes facing south and south-west above the town. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Münzlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 25.6 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Bernkastel include Graben, Lay, Alte Badstube am Doctorberg and Doctor.

appellations.name: Graacher Domprobst
appellations.summary: The Domprobst is Graach's steepest and most mineral site, named for the provost of Trier cathedral who once owned it. Willi Schaefer's fruity-sweet Kabinett and Spätlese from here are cult wines, with intense slate, citrus and herb flavours and a cool, pure finish; Kees-Kieren, Markus Molitor and S.A. Prüm also excel.
appellations.terroir: About 18 ha of deep blue and grey Devonian slate on a slope of up to 70 percent, south-west facing, with very thin topsoil that keeps yields low. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Münzlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 17.8 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Graach include Himmelreich, Abtsberg and Josephshöfer.
appellations.nerd_note: The old parcel name 'Graacher Abtsberg' within the slope recalls the abbey of St. Martin in Trier.

appellations.name: Graacher Himmelreich
appellations.summary: Graach's large Himmelreich ('kingdom of heaven'), about 57 ha, runs between the Domprobst and the Wehlener Sonnenuhr and gives some of the most charming fruity-sweet Kabinetts of the Mosel. Joh. Jos. Prüm, Dr. Loosen, Willi Schaefer and Selbach-Oster are reference growers. It is a classic source of the Mosel Kabinett archetype: around 8 percent alcohol, sweetness held in check by acidity, and flavours of green apple, white peach and wet slate.
appellations.terroir: Grey slate with more weathered loam than the Domprobst, giving softer, rounder wines on slopes facing south-west. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Münzlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 57.3 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Graach include Domprobst, Abtsberg and Josephshöfer.

appellations.name: Josephshöfer
appellations.summary: The Josephshöfer is the monopole of Reichsgraf von Kesselstatt, a walled site around the Josephshof manor between Graach and Wehlen that Kesselstatt acquired in the mid-nineteenth century. It gives full, ripe and spicy Riesling, slightly broader in build than the Sonnenuhr next door. Kesselstatt bottles it under the site name alone, from Kabinett to Grosses Gewächs, a rare case of a Mosel vineyard name standing without its village.
appellations.terroir: Deep weathered slate on a steep south-west-facing slope. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Münzlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages). Neighbouring sites in Graach include Himmelreich, Domprobst and Abtsberg.

appellations.name: Graacher Abtsberg
appellations.summary: A small, historic part of the Graach hillside once owned by St. Martin's abbey in Trier, bottled separately by a few estates.
appellations.terroir: Steep slate next to the Domprobst. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Münzlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 2.5 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Graach include Himmelreich, Domprobst and Josephshöfer.

appellations.name: Wehlener Sonnenuhr
appellations.summary: The Wehlener Sonnenuhr is the archetype of fruity-sweet Mosel Riesling: a steep, south-facing slope across the river from Wehlen, marked by a sundial that Jodocus Prüm built in 1842 so workers could tell the time. Joh. Jos. Prüm's Kabinett, Spätlese and Auslese from here are among the most collected white wines on earth, famous for their feather-light body, mineral spritz and capacity to age half a century. Dr. Loosen, S.A. Prüm, Selbach-Oster, Markus Molitor and Wegeler also own parcels.
appellations.terroir: About 43 ha of grey Devonian slate on slopes of up to 60 percent, facing south to south-west over a broad stretch of river, which reflects light and stores warmth; the slate warms the shallow soils and helps ripen grapes late into autumn. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Münzlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 42.6 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Wehlen include Klosterberg and Nonnenberg.
appellations.nerd_note: J.J. Prüm's wines are famous for a reductive, sulphury note when young, often mistaken for a fault; it fades with a few years in bottle.

appellations.name: Wehlener Nonnenberg
appellations.summary: A small Wehlen site of about 2.4 ha on the village side of the river, once owned by a convent, giving lighter Riesling.
appellations.terroir: Gentler slopes of slate and loam. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Münzlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 2.4 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Wehlen include Sonnenuhr and Klosterberg.

appellations.name: Wehlener Klosterberg
appellations.summary: A Wehlen site of about 14 ha behind the village, giving fresh, fruity Riesling.
appellations.terroir: Slate and loam, moderately steep. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Münzlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 14.3 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Wehlen include Sonnenuhr and Nonnenberg.

appellations.name: Zeltingen-Rachtiger Sonnenuhr
appellations.summary: Zeltingen's Sonnenuhr continues the Wehlener Sonnenuhr slope downstream and gives slightly broader, spicier wines. Selbach-Oster and Markus Molitor are the key growers, with old ungrafted vines. Zeltingen was long the largest wine village of the Middle Mosel. Selbach-Oster bottles its Rotlay parcel, ungrafted vines more than a century old, separately; the Sonnenuhr's wines are a touch broader than Wehlen's and age just as well.
appellations.terroir: About 18.5 ha of grey slate, steep and south-facing. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Münzlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 18.5 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Zeltingen-Rachtig include Himmelreich and Schloßberg.

appellations.name: Zeltingen-Rachtiger Schloßberg
appellations.summary: The Schlossberg rises behind Zeltingen around the site of a vanished castle. Selbach-Oster and Markus Molitor make powerful, spicy Riesling here, often dry.
appellations.terroir: About 17 ha of slate with more weathered rock and a south-east exposure. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Münzlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 16.7 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Zeltingen-Rachtig include Himmelreich and Sonnenuhr.

appellations.name: Zeltingen-Rachtiger Himmelreich
appellations.summary: A large Zeltingen site of about 80 ha, giving fruity, gentle Riesling.
appellations.terroir: Slate and loam on mixed slopes. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Münzlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 79.6 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Zeltingen-Rachtig include Schloßberg and Sonnenuhr.

appellations.name: Ürziger Würzgarten
appellations.summary: The Würzgarten ('spice garden') is a dramatic slope of red soil and slate cliffs above Ürzig, unlike anything else on the Mosel. Its Rieslings have a uniquely exotic spice, red fruits and a savoury, almost earthy depth. Many vines are ungrafted and very old, because phylloxera struggled in these soils. Dr. Loosen, Mönchhof, Jos. Christoffel, Rebenhof and Markus Molitor are key growers, and a tiny sundial parcel sits in the middle of the cliff.
appellations.terroir: About 51 ha where red Rotliegend sandstone and volcanic material overlie Devonian slate, giving red, iron-rich soils; the slope is terraced in places, south-facing and extremely steep, with walls and rock outcrops that store heat. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Schwarzlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 50.9 ha are registered under vine.
appellations.nerd_note: The red soils are a remnant of the Wittlich basin's Permian deposits, which reach the Mosel only at Ürzig and Erden.

appellations.name: Erdener Prälat
appellations.summary: The Prälat is one of the Mosel's smallest great sites, about 1.5 ha squeezed between red cliffs and the river below Erden. It is the warmest spot of the Middle Mosel: the rock walls store heat, the river reflects light and the vines face full south. Dr. Loosen's Auslese and Grosses Gewächs from here are rich, exotic and endlessly long, with spice from the red soils. Mönchhof and Jos. Christoffel also own parcels.
appellations.terroir: Red slate and weathered red sandstone in a narrow strip between a cliff and the water, with almost no frost and the earliest ripening of the area. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Schwarzlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 1.5 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Erden include Busslay and Treppchen.
appellations.nerd_note: Archaeologists excavated a Roman press house in Erden in the 1990s, below the Treppchen and Prälat, now partly reconstructed.

appellations.name: Erdener Treppchen
appellations.summary: The Treppchen ('little staircase') is named after the stone steps cut into the steep slope opposite Erden. Its Rieslings are firmer and more mineral than the Prälat, with blue slate and citrus. Dr. Loosen, Mönchhof, Markus Molitor and Jos. Christoffel make classic wines here. Erden sits on the inside of a bend, so its great vineyards lie across the river; Dr. Loosen's Treppchen Grosses Gewächs, from old own-rooted vines, is often the most mineral wine of his range.
appellations.terroir: About 36 ha of grey-blue Devonian slate on a very steep, south-west-facing slope. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Schwarzlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 36.3 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Erden include Busslay and Prälat.

appellations.name: Erdener Busslay
appellations.summary: A larger Erden site of about 59 ha downstream of the Treppchen, giving fruity, mineral Riesling, including from old vines.
appellations.terroir: Slate on a south-facing slope. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Schwarzlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 59 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Erden include Treppchen and Prälat.

appellations.name: Kinheimer Rosenberg
appellations.summary: A Kinheim slope of about 44 ha, giving lively, fruity Riesling of good value.
appellations.terroir: Slate on moderately steep slopes. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Schwarzlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 44.1 ha are registered under vine.

appellations.name: Wolfer Goldgrube
appellations.summary: The Goldgrube in Wolf was all but forgotten until the Swiss grower Daniel Vollenweider started reviving its terraces in 2000. Today it gives finely spiced, mineral Riesling, dry and sweet.
appellations.terroir: About 7 ha of steep slate terraces above Traben-Trarbach. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Schwarzlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 7 ha are registered under vine.

appellations.name: Trarbacher Hühnerberg
appellations.summary: A small, steep side-valley site in Trarbach, giving intense, cool Riesling, notably from Martin Müllen.
appellations.terroir: Slate in the Kautenbach valley, cooler than the main river. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Schwarzlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 2.5 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Trarbach include Ungsberg.

appellations.name: Trarbacher Ungsberg
appellations.summary: A tiny Trarbach site of under 2 ha, giving fine, fragrant Riesling from a handful of growers.
appellations.terroir: Steep slate above Trarbach. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Schwarzlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 1.9 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Trarbach include Hühnerberg.

appellations.name: Enkircher Batterieberg
appellations.summary: The Batterieberg is the monopole of Weingut Immich-Batterieberg in Enkirch. In the 1840s Carl August Immich blasted the slope out of rock with explosives, and the name recalls the 'battery' of charges. The wines are taut, smoky and long, mostly made in a dry or off-dry style.
appellations.terroir: About 1 ha of bare blue slate on an extremely steep, south-facing terrace. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Schwarzlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages). Neighbouring sites in Enkirch include Steffensberg, Ellergrub and Zeppwingert.

appellations.name: Enkircher Zeppwingert
appellations.summary: A steep Enkirch site of about 9 ha giving precise, mineral Riesling, notably from Immich-Batterieberg.
appellations.terroir: Grey slate on a south-west-facing slope. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Schwarzlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 9.2 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Enkirch include Steffensberg, Ellergrub and Batterieberg.

appellations.name: Enkircher Ellergrub
appellations.summary: The Ellergrub is a very steep, hot amphitheatre in Enkirch that Weiser-Künstler and Immich-Batterieberg have made famous again. Its Riesling is intense, spicy and deep.
appellations.terroir: About 6 ha of blue slate on a steep, south-facing bowl. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Schwarzlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 5.8 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Enkirch include Steffensberg, Zeppwingert and Batterieberg.

appellations.name: Enkircher Steffensberg
appellations.summary: A long Enkirch slope of about 30 ha, giving elegant, fruity Riesling, for example from Weiser-Künstler.
appellations.terroir: Slate on a south-facing slope. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Schwarzlay (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 30.3 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Enkirch include Ellergrub, Zeppwingert and Batterieberg.

appellations.name: Pündericher Marienburg
appellations.summary: The Marienburg rises opposite Pünderich below a ruined convent, a long, steep wall of slate that Clemens Busch has divided into parcels by rock type: blue slate in the Fahrlay, grey in the Falkenlay, red in the Rothenpfad and the old Raffes terraces. Each gives a different organic Riesling, from cool and mineral to warm and spicy, a lesson in how slate colour changes wine.
appellations.terroir: About 50 ha of grey, blue and red Devonian slate on very steep south to south-west slopes, many still terraced with dry-stone walls. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bernkastel and the Grosslage Vom heißen Stein (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 50.2 ha are registered under vine.
appellations.nerd_note: Busch's parcel bottlings revived historic names that the 1971 law had merged into the single Marienburg.

appellations.name: Calmont
appellations.summary: The Calmont, between Bremm and Ediger-Eller, is often called the steepest vineyard in Europe, with gradients of up to 65 degrees on a cliff of slate and quartzite above a tight loop of the Mosel. Much of it was abandoned in the late twentieth century; growers such as Weingut Franzen in Bremm have brought terraces back into production. The wines are concentrated, ripe and spicy, with a cool mineral line from the rock. A via ferrata (Calmont Klettersteig) crosses the slope.
appellations.terroir: About 18 ha under vine on a south-facing wall of Devonian slate and quartzite; the rock and the river make it one of the warmest sites of the lower Mosel despite its northerly position. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Burg Cochem and the Grosslage Grafschaft (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 18.2 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Bremm include Frauenberg.
appellations.nerd_note: Archaeologists have found the remains of a Gallo-Roman temple on the summit; the name is often derived from Latin calidus mons, 'warm mountain'.

appellations.name: Frauenberg
appellations.summary: A steep site shared by Bremm and Neef, opposite the Calmont, named after the ruined Stuben convent below it. It gives ripe, slatey Riesling.
appellations.terroir: About 14.5 ha of steep slate. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Burg Cochem and the Grosslage Grafschaft (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 14.5 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Bremm include Calmont.

appellations.name: Neefer Petersberg
appellations.summary: A small, steep Neef site under the chapel of St. Peter, giving firm, mineral Riesling.
appellations.terroir: Slate on a south-facing slope. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Burg Cochem and the Grosslage Grafschaft (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 7.7 ha are registered under vine.

appellations.name: Valwiger Herrenberg
appellations.summary: A steep Valwig slope of about 18 ha in a loop of the river near Cochem, giving spicy, rich Riesling.
appellations.terroir: Terraced slate on a south-facing bend. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Burg Cochem and the Grosslage Rosenhang (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 17.9 ha are registered under vine.

appellations.name: Cochemer Pinnerkreuzberg
appellations.summary: A steep site behind Cochem named after a wayside cross, giving cool, firm Riesling.
appellations.terroir: Slate above the town, facing south. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Burg Cochem and the Grosslage Goldbäumchen (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages).

appellations.name: Hatzenporter Kirchberg
appellations.summary: The Kirchberg rises behind the church at Hatzenport, a steep, terraced slope where Heymann-Löwenstein makes a dense, spicy dry Riesling. It sits on the Terrassenmosel, the lowest stretch of the Mosel, where dry-stone terraces are the only way to hold soil on the rock.
appellations.terroir: About 5.7 ha of terraced Devonian slate and sandstone, south-facing. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Burg Cochem and the Grosslage Weinhex (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 5.7 ha are registered under vine.

appellations.name: Uhlen
appellations.summary: The Uhlen is the great site of Winningen, a long, terraced cliff above the lower Mosel. Reinhard Löwenstein of Heymann-Löwenstein argued for decades that its three sections have different rocks and should be named separately; the EU now protects Uhlen Blaufüßer Lay, Uhlen Laubach and Uhlen Roth Lay as designations of their own. The wines are dense, often powerful dry Rieslings with smoke, herbs and a salty finish. Knebel and Lubentiushof also excel.
appellations.terroir: About 14 ha registered under vine on steep terraces of Devonian slate: blue slate in the Blaufüßer Lay, fossil-rich grey slate and limestone bands in the Laubach, red iron-rich slate in the Roth Lay. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Burg Cochem and the Grosslage Weinhex (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 14.4 ha are registered under vine.
appellations.nerd_note: The fossil beds of the Laubach section contain Devonian marine creatures, a reminder that the slate began as ocean mud around 400 million years ago.

appellations.name: Winningener Brückstück
appellations.summary: A Winningen site of about 8 ha by the old bridge, giving lively, mineral Riesling, for example from Knebel.
appellations.terroir: Terraced slate on the lower Mosel. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Burg Cochem and the Grosslage Weinhex (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 8 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Winningen include Hamm.

appellations.name: Winningener Hamm
appellations.summary: A steep Winningen slope of about 11.5 ha, giving firm, fruity Riesling.
appellations.terroir: Slate terraces above the village. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Burg Cochem and the Grosslage Weinhex (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 11.5 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Winningen include Brückstück.

appellations.name: Röttgen
appellations.summary: The Röttgen, shared by Winningen and Güls, is a steep terraced site whose Rieslings are spicy and complex, made famously dry by Heymann-Löwenstein and Knebel.
appellations.terroir: About 10.6 ha of slate terraces, south-facing. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Burg Cochem and the Grosslage Weinhex (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 10.6 ha are registered under vine.

appellations.name: Lehmener Würzlay
appellations.summary: A small terraced Lehmen site of about 6 ha, giving spicy, ripe Riesling.
appellations.terroir: Slate terraces on the lower Mosel. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Burg Cochem and the Grosslage Weinhex (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 5.9 ha are registered under vine.

appellations.name: Nitteler Leiterchen
appellations.summary: The Leiterchen is the best-known site of the Upper Mosel, where the river forms the border with Luxembourg and Devonian slate gives way to Triassic shell limestone (Muschelkalk). It is a stronghold of Elbling, the ancient Roman-era variety of the area, giving crisp, citric still and sparkling wines.
appellations.terroir: About 38 ha of limestone and marl on south-facing slopes, a geology closer to Burgundy and Champagne than to the rest of the Mosel. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Obermosel and the Grosslage Gipfel (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 38.4 ha are registered under vine.
appellations.nerd_note: Elbling has been grown here for nearly 2,000 years; the Upper Mosel is its last real home in Germany.

appellations.name: Niederhausener Hermannshöhle
appellations.summary: The Hermannshöhle is the Nahe's most celebrated vineyard, a steep, south-facing slope above the river at Niederhausen where an astonishing mix of rocks meets in a few hectares. Helmut and Cornelius Dönnhoff made it famous worldwide, and their Grosses Gewächs and fruity-sweet Spätlese from here combine Mosel-like delicacy with a deeper, spicier, more mineral core. Jakob Schneider and Gut Hermannsberg also own parcels. Prussian-era tax classifications of the Nahe already placed it in the top class.
appellations.terroir: About 8.4 ha under vine on grey slate interleaved with volcanic porphyry (rhyolite), melaphyre and bands of limestone; the slope faces south and south-west over the Nahe, which reflects light and keeps frost away. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Burgweg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 8.4 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Niederhausen include Klamm, Hermannsberg, Rosenheck and Steinberg.
appellations.nerd_note: Few vineyards anywhere pack so many rock types into so small an area, which helps explain why the Hermannshöhle tastes more layered than its neighbours.

appellations.name: Niederhausener Hermannsberg
appellations.summary: The Hermannsberg is the monopole of Gut Hermannsberg, founded in 1902 as the Prussian State Domain at Niederhausen. Labourers, including prisoners, blasted terraces out of the rock to create model vineyards, and the estate was one of Germany's most famous until its decline after the 1990s; new owners have restored it since 2009. The Riesling is powerful, spicy and stony.
appellations.terroir: Volcanic rock and slate terraces on a steep slope above the Nahe. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Burgweg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages). Neighbouring sites in Niederhausen include Klamm, Hermannshöhle, Rosenheck and Steinberg.
appellations.nerd_note: The domain's wines were the Prussian state's showcase for what scientific viticulture could do on abandoned slopes.

appellations.name: Niederhausener Klamm
appellations.summary: A small Niederhausen site of about 7.5 ha in a narrow gorge ('Klamm'), giving taut, cool Riesling.
appellations.terroir: Slate and volcanic rock in a shaded side valley. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Burgweg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 7.5 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Niederhausen include Hermannsberg, Hermannshöhle, Rosenheck and Steinberg.

appellations.name: Niederhausener Rosenheck
appellations.summary: A Niederhausen site of about 9.6 ha above the river, giving fragrant, fine Riesling for several estates.
appellations.terroir: Porphyry and slate on a south-facing slope. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Burgweg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 9.6 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Niederhausen include Klamm, Hermannsberg, Hermannshöhle and Steinberg.

appellations.name: Niederhausener Steinberg
appellations.summary: A Niederhausen site of about 5.6 ha that belongs in part to Gut Hermannsberg, giving firm, mineral Riesling.
appellations.terroir: Volcanic and slate soils on a steep slope. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Burgweg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 5.6 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Niederhausen include Klamm, Hermannsberg, Hermannshöhle and Rosenheck.

appellations.name: Oberhausener Brücke
appellations.summary: The Brücke is a tiny monopole of Dönnhoff next to the old bridge at Oberhausen, barely a hectare on the river bank. It is known for grippy, smoky Riesling and for Eiswein, because cold air settles over the water here on winter nights. It is one of the very few true monopoles of the Nahe.
appellations.terroir: Grey slate with loess and loam on a low, flat site right on the Nahe; the river both protects it in autumn and chills it in winter. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Burgweg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages). Neighbouring sites in Oberhausen include Leistenberg.
appellations.nerd_note: Dönnhoff's Brücke Eisweins are among the most celebrated of the 1990s and 2000s.

appellations.name: Oberhausener Leistenberg
appellations.summary: A steep slate slope in Oberhausen of about 5 ha, where Dönnhoff makes a vibrant, fruity Riesling Kabinett.
appellations.terroir: Grey slate, south-facing, in a side valley. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Burgweg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 4.9 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Oberhausen include Brücke.

appellations.name: Schloßböckelheimer Felsenberg
appellations.summary: The Felsenberg ('rock hill') is a steep, rocky slope at Schlossböckelheim, the source of some of the Nahe's most precise dry Rieslings from Dönnhoff and Schäfer-Fröhlich. The wines are cool, smoky and intensely mineral, with herbal notes from the volcanic soils. The village takes its name from Böckelheim castle, where Emperor Henry IV was imprisoned by his own son in 1105; the castle ruins still crown the hill.
appellations.terroir: About 10.6 ha of weathered rhyolite (porphyry) with little soil, on steep south-facing slopes above the Nahe. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Burgweg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 10.6 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Schloßböckelheim include In den Felsen and Kupfergrube.

appellations.name: Schloßböckelheimer Kupfergrube
appellations.summary: The Kupfergrube ('copper mine') takes its name from old copper workings in the hillside. Early in the twentieth century the Prussian state domain cleared and terraced it, and it quickly became one of the Nahe's grand sites. Schäfer-Fröhlich and Gut Hermannsberg make tense, smoky, spicy Riesling here.
appellations.terroir: About 12.6 ha of volcanic rock (melaphyre and rhyolite) on steep terraces facing south. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Burgweg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 12.6 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Schloßböckelheim include Felsenberg and In den Felsen.
appellations.nerd_note: Before it was planted the hill was covered with scrub; the domain proved that a site with no vineyard history could become a grand cru in one generation.

appellations.name: Schloßböckelheimer In den Felsen
appellations.summary: A small Schlossböckelheim site of about 6.5 ha among rock outcrops, giving fine, stony Riesling.
appellations.terroir: Porphyry rock with thin soils. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Burgweg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 6.5 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Schloßböckelheim include Felsenberg and Kupfergrube.

appellations.name: Traisener Bastei
appellations.summary: The Bastei is a narrow strip of vines at the foot of the Rotenfels, the tallest rock face between the Alps and Scandinavia, about 200 m of red rhyolite. Only about 1.7 ha are planted, on scree that has fallen from the cliff; Dr. Crusius makes an intense, smoky, almost spicy Riesling from it, among the warmest sites of the Nahe.
appellations.terroir: Rhyolite scree at the base of a south-facing cliff that stores and radiates heat onto the vines. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Burgweg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 1.7 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Traisen include Rotenfels.
appellations.nerd_note: Climbers and hikers on the Rotenfels look straight down onto the Bastei; the cliff is a nature reserve.

appellations.name: Traisener Rotenfels
appellations.summary: A Traisen site of about 16 ha below and beside the Rotenfels cliff, giving ripe, spicy Riesling, notably from Dr. Crusius.
