appellations.terroir: Red rhyolite and weathered volcanic soils. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Burgweg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 15.8 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Traisen include Bastei.

appellations.name: Norheimer Dellchen
appellations.summary: The Dellchen is a steep, terraced slope of about 3 ha above Norheim, divided by dry-stone walls and rock outcrops. Dönnhoff's Grosses Gewächs from here is often his most aromatic, with white flowers, herbs and a cool, stony finish. Some terraces were abandoned in the late twentieth century because they could only be worked by hand; Dönnhoff and others have brought parcels back into production.
appellations.terroir: Grey slate mixed with porphyry and melaphyre on small terraces facing south over the Nahe. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Burgweg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 3.1 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Norheim include Kafels and Kirschheck.

appellations.name: Norheimer Kafels
appellations.summary: The Kafels is a steep Norheim slope where volcanic rock dominates, giving spicy, mineral Riesling, for example from Jakob Schneider.
appellations.terroir: Volcanic soils on a south-facing slope. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Burgweg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages). Neighbouring sites in Norheim include Kirschheck and Dellchen.

appellations.name: Norheimer Kirschheck
appellations.summary: The Kirschheck in Norheim gives a lighter, fragrant style of Riesling; Dönnhoff's Kirschheck Spätlese is a byword for finesse.
appellations.terroir: About 13 ha of grey slate on a steep slope. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Burgweg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 13.4 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Norheim include Kafels and Dellchen.

appellations.name: Monzingener Halenberg
appellations.summary: The Halenberg is the great site of Emrich-Schönleber, a very steep slope above Monzingen on the upper Nahe. Its blue slate and quartzite give some of Germany's most electric dry Rieslings: cool, smoky, salty and very long, plus spectacular sweet wines. Schönleber's Halenberg GG is regularly cited among the best dry Rieslings of the country.
appellations.terroir: About 8 ha of blue Devonian slate with quartzite on a south-facing slope of up to 70 percent, higher and cooler than the middle Nahe. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Paradiesgarten (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 8.3 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Monzingen include Frühlingsplätzchen.
appellations.nerd_note: Monzingen lies on the edge of the Hunsrück; the cool winds and the slate give the Halenberg a Mosel-like nerve with Nahe depth.

appellations.name: Monzingener Frühlingsplätzchen
appellations.summary: The Frühlingsplätzchen ('little spring place') is Monzingen's second great site, warmer and softer than the Halenberg, with red slate and loam. Emrich-Schönleber's wines from here are juicy and generous.
appellations.terroir: About 70 ha registered, red slate, quartzite and loam on south-facing slopes. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Paradiesgarten (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 69.7 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Monzingen include Halenberg.
appellations.nerd_note: The name refers to the early bud-break of this sheltered slope.

appellations.name: Kreuznacher Kahlenberg
appellations.summary: The Kahlenberg is a Bad Kreuznach slope of about 17 ha on gravel, loam and sandstone, giving full, fruity Riesling, notably from Dönnhoff and Kreuznach estates.
appellations.terroir: Weathered sandstone, gravel and loam on south-facing slopes on the edge of the spa town. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Kronenberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 16.9 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Bad Kreuznach include Brückes and Krötenpfuhl.

appellations.name: Kreuznacher Krötenpfuhl
appellations.summary: The Krötenpfuhl ('toad pond') in Bad Kreuznach gives a creamy, ripe Riesling on deep gravel and loam, a very different face of the Nahe from the volcanic sites upstream. Dönnhoff's Krötenpfuhl is a reference.
appellations.terroir: About 6.4 ha of gravel, loess and clay on a gentle slope. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Kronenberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 6.4 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Bad Kreuznach include Kahlenberg and Brückes.

appellations.name: Kreuznacher Brückes
appellations.summary: A Bad Kreuznach site of about 6.4 ha with deep loess and sandstone soils, giving rich, aromatic Riesling for town estates.
appellations.terroir: Loess and sandstone near the centre of Bad Kreuznach. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Kronenberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 6.4 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Bad Kreuznach include Kahlenberg and Krötenpfuhl.

appellations.name: Dorsheimer Goldloch
appellations.summary: The Goldloch ('gold hole') at Dorsheim is one of the three great sites of Schlossgut Diel, a warm amphitheatre of stony soils giving opulent, spicy Riesling, both dry and fruity-sweet.
appellations.terroir: About 10 ha of gravelly loam over quartzite and slate in a sheltered bowl. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Schlosskapelle (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 10.4 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Dorsheim include Burgberg and Pittermännchen.

appellations.name: Dorsheimer Pittermännchen
appellations.summary: The Pittermännchen is a small, steep Dorsheim slope of slate and quartzite where Schlossgut Diel makes a fine, cool, citrus-driven Riesling. The odd name is said to recall a small silver coin, the Pittermännchen, once paid for the land.
appellations.terroir: About 7.4 ha of slate and quartzite on a steep slope facing south-west. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Schlosskapelle (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 7.4 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Dorsheim include Burgberg and Goldloch.

appellations.name: Dorsheimer Burgberg
appellations.summary: A small Dorsheim site of about 3.8 ha below a castle, giving concentrated, mineral Riesling from Schlossgut Diel.
appellations.terroir: Stony quartzite and slate on a steep slope. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Schlosskapelle (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 3.8 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Dorsheim include Goldloch and Pittermännchen.

appellations.name: Rümmelsheimer Schloßberg
appellations.summary: The slope below the castle of Burg Layen in Rümmelsheim, home of Schlossgut Diel, giving fine, mineral Riesling that Diel sells as Burg Layener Schlossberg.
appellations.terroir: About 15 ha of quartzite and slate on south-facing slopes. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Schlosskapelle (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 15 ha are registered under vine.

appellations.name: Laubenheimer Karthäuser
appellations.summary: A Laubenheim site of about 18 ha once owned by Carthusian monks, made famous by Martin Tesch with taut, unadorned dry Riesling.
appellations.terroir: Weathered quartzite and loam on south-facing slopes. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Schlosskapelle (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 18.4 ha are registered under vine.

appellations.name: Langenlonsheimer Rothenberg
appellations.summary: A Langenlonsheim slope of about 10 ha with red, iron-rich soils, giving warm, spicy Riesling from Tesch and others.
appellations.terroir: Red sandstone and loam (Rotliegend) on a south-facing slope. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Schlosskapelle (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 9.9 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Langenlonsheim include Königsschild.

appellations.name: Langenlonsheimer Königsschild
appellations.summary: A Langenlonsheim site of about 15 ha, giving bright, fruity Riesling, notably for Tesch's single-vineyard range.
appellations.terroir: Loam over gravel and quartzite. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Schlosskapelle (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 15.1 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Langenlonsheim include Rothenberg.

appellations.name: Münster-Sarmsheimer Dautenpflänzer
appellations.summary: A small, steep site of about 4 ha in Münster-Sarmsheim at the mouth of the Nahe, where Kruger-Rumpf makes a spicy, mineral Riesling with real tension.
appellations.terroir: Slate and quartzite on a steep south-facing slope near the Rhine. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Schlosskapelle (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 4 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Münster-Sarmsheim include Pittersberg.

appellations.name: Münster-Sarmsheimer Pittersberg
appellations.summary: A Münster-Sarmsheim site of about 9 ha of blue slate giving cool, elegant Riesling, notably from Kruger-Rumpf.
appellations.terroir: Blue slate on a steep slope. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Schlosskapelle (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 9.4 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Münster-Sarmsheim include Dautenpflänzer.

appellations.name: Bockenauer Felseneck
appellations.summary: The Felseneck is a very steep, rocky slope in the Ellerbach valley at Bockenau, a side valley north of the Nahe. Tim Fröhlich of Schäfer-Fröhlich turned this once-obscure site into one of Germany's most sought-after dry Rieslings: smoky, wild-yeast fermented, crystalline and intense.
appellations.terroir: About 10 ha of blue and grey Devonian slate on a steep south-facing slope, cooler and higher than the main Nahe valley. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Rosengarten (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 10.4 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Bockenau include Stromberg.
appellations.nerd_note: Bockenau had no reputation before Schäfer-Fröhlich; the Felseneck shows how much the German wine map has been redrawn by growers since 2000.

appellations.name: Bockenauer Stromberg
appellations.summary: A small Bockenau slope of slate where Schäfer-Fröhlich makes a cooler, tighter Grosses Gewächs than the Felseneck.
appellations.terroir: Grey slate on a steep, high slope. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Rosengarten (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages). Neighbouring sites in Bockenau include Felseneck.

appellations.name: Wallhausener Johannisberg
appellations.summary: The Johannisberg at Wallhausen is a home site of Prinz Salm, an estate whose family has made wine here for centuries and claims one of Germany's longest unbroken wine-growing lineages. It gives fine, floral Riesling on mixed soils.
appellations.terroir: About 11 ha of slate, quartzite and loam in the Gräfenbach valley. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Pfarrgarten (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 10.8 ha are registered under vine.

appellations.name: Odernheimer Kloster Disibodenberg
appellations.summary: This small site surrounds the ruins of the Disibodenberg monastery above Odernheim, where Hildegard of Bingen lived as a nun from 1112 until about 1150. Monks planted vines here in the Middle Ages, and today a single estate works about 7 ha.
appellations.terroir: South-facing slopes of red sandstone and volcanic soils around the abbey ruins at the meeting of the Nahe and Glan. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Paradiesgarten (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 7.1 ha are registered under vine.
appellations.nerd_note: Hildegard wrote about wine as medicine, and the Disibodenberg is one of the few places where you can stand in her vineyard.

appellations.name: Abtei Rupertsberg
appellations.summary: The Abtei Rupertsberg site at Bingerbrück recalls the convent Hildegard of Bingen founded on the Rupertsberg around 1150 after leaving the Disibodenberg. A few hectares of vines grow on the hill where the Nahe meets the Rhine.
appellations.terroir: Quartzite and slate on slopes above the confluence. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Schlosskapelle (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 4.7 ha are registered under vine.

appellations.name: Meddersheimer Rheingrafenberg
appellations.summary: A Meddersheim site of about 28 ha, named after the Rhinegraves who ruled the area, giving fresh, fruity Riesling, notably for the local cooperative and family estates.
appellations.terroir: Volcanic and sandstone soils on south-facing slopes of the upper Nahe. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nahetal and the Grosslage Paradiesgarten (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 28.4 ha are registered under vine.

appellations.name: Niersteiner Pettenthal
appellations.summary: The Pettenthal is the steepest and most famous part of the Roter Hang, the 'red slope' that runs along the Rhine north of Nierstein. Its Rieslings are exotic and dense, with peach, blood orange and a savoury, iron-tinged mineral finish. Kühling-Gillot, Keller, St. Antony, Gunderloch and Schätzel are among the owners; the wines rank with the finest dry Rieslings of Germany.
appellations.terroir: About 30 ha of red Rotliegend clay-slate and siltstone (Permian, about 280 million years old) on slopes of up to 70 percent, facing east and south-east straight over the Rhine, which reflects morning light onto the vines. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nierstein and the Grosslage Rehbach (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 30.1 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Nierstein include Paterberg, Ölberg, Hipping and Heiligenbaum.
appellations.nerd_note: The red rock was laid down in a hot desert basin; it crumbles into fine, iron-rich soil that warms quickly and drains well.

appellations.name: Niersteiner Hipping
appellations.summary: The Hipping is the heart of the Roter Hang right above Nierstein, a steep slope of red soil whose Rieslings are fine, spicy and long, a touch more elegant than the Pettenthal. Klaus Peter Keller's Hipping has become one of the most sought-after dry Rieslings of the Rhine; Schätzel and St. Antony also excel. In the nineteenth century the wines of Nierstein's red slope were sold at prices to rival the Rheingau's best, a reputation the 1971 Grosslage 'Niersteiner Gutes Domtal' did much to erode.
appellations.terroir: About 23 ha of red Rotliegend clay-slate on an east to south-east-facing slope. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nierstein and the Grosslage Rehbach (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 22.7 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Nierstein include Paterberg, Ölberg, Pettenthal and Heiligenbaum.

appellations.name: Niersteiner Brudersberg
appellations.summary: The Brudersberg is a small, steep monopole on the Roter Hang, long the pride of the Heyl zu Herrnsheim estate and now worked by St. Antony. It gives firm, spicy Riesling.
appellations.terroir: Red Rotliegend soils on a steep south-east slope. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nierstein and the Grosslage Rehbach (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages). Neighbouring sites in Nierstein include Paterberg, Ölberg, Pettenthal and Hipping.

appellations.name: Niersteiner Ölberg
appellations.summary: The Ölberg ('olive hill') is a warm, steep slope in Nierstein that gives rich, round Riesling with ripe stone fruit, made by Keller, Schätzel, Huff and others.
appellations.terroir: About 47 ha of red Rotliegend soils and some limestone, south-east facing. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nierstein and the Grosslage Auflangen (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 47.4 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Nierstein include Paterberg, Pettenthal, Hipping and Heiligenbaum.

appellations.name: Orbel
appellations.summary: The Orbel, shared by Nierstein and Schwabsburg, lies behind the Roter Hang on red soil and gives spicy, ripe Riesling.
appellations.terroir: About 12 ha of Rotliegend soils. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nierstein and the Grosslage Auflangen (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 12.2 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Nierstein include Paterberg, Ölberg, Pettenthal and Hipping.

appellations.name: Niersteiner Heiligenbaum
appellations.summary: A Nierstein site of about 12.5 ha named after a holy tree, giving lively, fruity Riesling.
appellations.terroir: Red soils and loess on gentler slopes. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nierstein and the Grosslage Auflangen (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 12.5 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Nierstein include Paterberg, Ölberg, Pettenthal and Hipping.

appellations.name: Niersteiner Paterberg
appellations.summary: A large Nierstein site of about 118 ha behind the town, giving ripe, everyday Riesling and Silvaner.
appellations.terroir: Loess and limestone on rolling slopes. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nierstein and the Grosslage Spiegelberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 118.2 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Nierstein include Ölberg, Pettenthal, Hipping and Heiligenbaum.

appellations.name: Niersteiner Glöck
appellations.summary: The Glöck is a small walled vineyard by St. Kilian's church in Nierstein, often called the oldest documented vineyard in Germany: a charter of 742 records its gift to the bishopric of Würzburg.
appellations.terroir: A walled urban site on loess and red soils. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nierstein and the Grosslage Auflangen (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages). Neighbouring sites in Nierstein include Paterberg, Ölberg, Pettenthal and Hipping.
appellations.nerd_note: The 742 donation was made by Carloman, a son of Charles Martel.

appellations.name: Nackenheimer Rothenberg
appellations.summary: The Rothenberg is the northern end of the Roter Hang at Nackenheim, the steepest and reddest of its slopes. Gunderloch made it famous in the 1990s with spectacular sweet Rieslings, and Kühling-Gillot farms ungrafted vines here. The wines are intense, spicy and long-lived. Nackenheim is the birthplace of the playwright Carl Zuckmayer, whose comedy 'Der fröhliche Weinberg' (1925) is set among Rheinhessen vineyards.
appellations.terroir: About 14.5 ha of red Rotliegend clay-slate on steep east-facing slopes above the Rhine. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nierstein and the Grosslage Spiegelberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 14.5 ha are registered under vine.
appellations.nerd_note: Kühling-Gillot still farms very old own-rooted vines here, rare on the Rhine.

appellations.name: Oppenheimer Sackträger
appellations.summary: The Sackträger ('sack carrier') is Oppenheim's best-known site, on limestone and loess above the old town, giving full, elegant Riesling and Silvaner.
appellations.terroir: About 19 ha of limestone, marl and loess, facing south-east. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nierstein and the Grosslage Güldenmorgen (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 19.3 ha are registered under vine.
appellations.nerd_note: Oppenheim's medieval cellars form a labyrinth of passages under the town, now partly open to visitors.

appellations.name: Kreuz
appellations.summary: The Kreuz, shared by Dienheim and Oppenheim, is a broad slope of loess and limestone giving ripe, round white wines.
appellations.terroir: About 49 ha of loess over limestone. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nierstein and the Grosslage Güldenmorgen (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 48.9 ha are registered under vine.

appellations.name: Burgweg
appellations.summary: The Burgweg, shared by Bodenheim and Mainz-Laubenheim, is a home site of Kühling-Gillot, giving firm, mineral Riesling on limestone.
appellations.terroir: About 41 ha of limestone, marl and loess. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Nierstein and the Grosslage Sankt Alban (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 41.3 ha are registered under vine.

appellations.name: Westhofener Morstein
appellations.summary: The Morstein is the jewel of Westhofen and one of the great Rieslings sites of Germany, a gentle south-facing slope on the edge of the Wonnegau hills. Philipp Wittmann and Klaus Peter Keller make powerful, chiselled dry Rieslings here, with yellow fruit, herbs and a long chalky finish; they age for decades. Gutzler and Groebe are also important.
appellations.terroir: Clay marl over fissured limestone, with deep roots reaching water even in dry summers; the slope is open to the south and fairly high for Rheinhessen, which keeps acidity firm. About 150 ha are registered in the wider Einzellage, though the classic core is much smaller. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Wonnegau and the Grosslage Bergkloster (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 152.5 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Westhofen include Steingrube, Aulerde, Kirchspiel and Brunnenhäuschen.
appellations.nerd_note: Before the 1990s Westhofen was known for bulk wine; the Morstein became a symbol of the Rheinhessen revolution led by young growers.

appellations.name: Westhofener Kirchspiel
appellations.summary: The Kirchspiel is a Westhofen amphitheatre facing south-east towards the village church, giving finely fruited, elegant dry Riesling from Wittmann, Keller and Groebe. Kirchspiel means 'parish', a reminder of church ownership. Wittmann farms biodynamically, and his Kirchspiel Grosses Gewächs is often the most elegant of his three Westhofen grand sites: the amphitheatre concentrates warmth while the limestone keeps the wine tight.
appellations.terroir: About 44 ha of limestone and marl in a sheltered bowl. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Wonnegau and the Grosslage Bergkloster (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 43.8 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Westhofen include Morstein, Steingrube, Aulerde and Brunnenhäuschen.

appellations.name: Westhofener Brunnenhäuschen
appellations.summary: The Brunnenhäuschen ('little well house') sits high above Westhofen on red-tinged limestone soils. Keller's Abtserde, one of Germany's most coveted Rieslings, comes from a parcel inside it; Wittmann also bottles a Grosses Gewächs. It is the highest of the Westhofen grand sites, and its wines tend to be the most tightly wound when young.
appellations.terroir: About 31 ha of terra rossa-like reddish clay over limestone, the highest part of Westhofen. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Wonnegau and the Grosslage Bergkloster (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 31.1 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Westhofen include Morstein, Steingrube, Aulerde and Kirchspiel.
appellations.nerd_note: Abtserde ('abbot's earth') recalls medieval monastic ownership of the parcel.

appellations.name: Westhofener Aulerde
appellations.summary: The Aulerde lies on lower, warmer ground in Westhofen with sandy loam and gravel, giving generous, juicy Riesling from Wittmann and Gutzler.
appellations.terroir: About 100 ha of loam, sand and gravel. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Wonnegau and the Grosslage Bergkloster (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 102.4 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Westhofen include Morstein, Steingrube, Kirchspiel and Brunnenhäuschen.

appellations.name: Westhofener Steingrube
appellations.summary: A large Westhofen site of about 144 ha on limestone, giving fresh white and red wines, with Pinot Noir from some growers.
appellations.terroir: Limestone and marl on gentle slopes. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Wonnegau and the Grosslage Bergkloster (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 144 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Westhofen include Morstein, Aulerde, Kirchspiel and Brunnenhäuschen.

appellations.name: Dalsheimer Hubacker
appellations.summary: The Hubacker is the founding site of Weingut Keller in Flörsheim-Dalsheim, a gentle limestone slope that helped make Klaus and Klaus Peter Keller famous. Its dry Riesling is concentrated, mineral and slow to open. The Keller family has farmed in Flörsheim-Dalsheim since 1789. Their cult Riesling G-Max is sold without a site name, and the estate keeps its exact source secret.
appellations.terroir: About 23 ha of limestone with thin clay marl, facing south-east. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Wonnegau and the Grosslage Burg Rodenstein (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 22.8 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Dalsheim include Bürgel.

appellations.name: Dalsheimer Bürgel
appellations.summary: A large Dalsheim site of about 84 ha on limestone where Keller grows outstanding Pinot Noir and Silvaner as well as Riesling.
appellations.terroir: Limestone and marl with some loess. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Wonnegau and the Grosslage Burg Rodenstein (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 83.9 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Dalsheim include Hubacker.

appellations.name: Nieder-Flörsheimer Frauenberg
appellations.summary: The Frauenberg at Nieder-Flörsheim is a high limestone hill where Keller and Battenfeld-Spanier grow cool, precise Riesling and Pinot Noir.
appellations.terroir: Limestone with little soil on a high, windy plateau edge. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Wonnegau and the Grosslage Burg Rodenstein (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 150.2 ha are registered under vine.

appellations.name: Hohen-Sülzener Kirchenstück
appellations.summary: The Kirchenstück at Hohen-Sülzen is a limestone site that Battenfeld-Spanier has made famous with taut, saline dry Riesling.
appellations.terroir: About 98 ha registered, limestone and marl on south-facing slopes on the border with the Pfalz. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Wonnegau and the Grosslage Domblick (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 98.3 ha are registered under vine.

appellations.name: Mölsheimer Zellerweg am Schwarzen Herrgott
appellations.summary: This site with one of Germany's longest vineyard names, 'the Zell path by the black crucifix', lies at Mölsheim on the border with the Pfalz. Battenfeld-Spanier makes a cool, limestone-driven Riesling here.
appellations.terroir: About 56 ha of limestone on a high plateau. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Wonnegau and the Grosslage Domblick (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 55.8 ha are registered under vine.

appellations.name: Wormser Liebfrauenstift-Kirchenstück
appellations.summary: This walled vineyard surrounds the Liebfrauenkirche in Worms, the church whose 'Liebfrauenmilch' gave its name to Germany's most famous and most debased wine style. Today a handful of estates make serious dry Riesling from the 12.5 ha around the church. The Gothic church rises out of the vines in the middle of the city, one of the very few urban grand sites in Germany.
appellations.terroir: Gravelly loam on the Rhine plain, sheltered by the church and town. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Wonnegau and the Grosslage Liebfrauenmorgen (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 12.5 ha are registered under vine.
appellations.nerd_note: In the eighteenth and nineteenth centuries 'Liebfrauenmilch' meant the wine of this specific site; the name later spread to oceans of sweet blends.

appellations.name: Siefersheimer Höllberg
appellations.summary: The Höllberg at Siefersheim is a high, rocky site of volcanic porphyry in the 'Rheinhessian Switzerland', the hilly west of the region. Wagner-Stempel makes a cool, smoky, very mineral Riesling here. The name is usually read as 'hell hill', after the heat that builds up on its rocks.
appellations.terroir: About 29 ha of rhyolite (porphyry) rubble on a south-facing slope at up to about 300 m. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bingen and the Grosslage Rheingrafenstein (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 28.9 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Siefersheim include Goldenes Horn.
appellations.nerd_note: Porphyry links Siefersheim geologically to the neighbouring Nahe rather than to the limestone of the Wonnegau.

appellations.name: Heerkretz
appellations.summary: The Heerkretz, shared by Siefersheim and Neu-Bamberg, is a steep, rocky slope of porphyry giving intense, smoky Riesling, the flagship of Wagner-Stempel. Daniel Wagner of Wagner-Stempel turned these remote western hills of Rheinhessen into a Grosses Gewächs address; the porphyry gives a smoky, saline character closer to the Nahe than to the limestone of the Wonnegau.
appellations.terroir: About 58 ha of rhyolite rock and thin soils on south-facing slopes. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bingen and the Grosslage Rheingrafenstein (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 58.2 ha are registered under vine.

appellations.name: Siefersheimer Goldenes Horn
appellations.summary: A Siefersheim site of about 75 ha on volcanic and sandy soils, giving fresh, fruity white wines.
appellations.terroir: Porphyry and sand in the western hills. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bingen and the Grosslage Rheingrafenstein (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 74.9 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Siefersheim include Höllberg.

appellations.name: Ober-Ingelheimer Pares
appellations.summary: The Pares at Ober-Ingelheim is a limestone site long celebrated for Pinot Noir; Ingelheim calls itself the 'red wine town' and its Spätburgunder tradition goes back to the Middle Ages. J. Neus is the reference producer.
appellations.terroir: About 9 ha of limestone and marl on south-facing slopes. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bingen and the Grosslage Kaiserpfalz (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 9 ha are registered under vine.
appellations.nerd_note: Charlemagne built a palace at Ingelheim; legend says that from here he saw the snow melt first on the slopes across the Rhine and ordered them planted with vines.

appellations.name: Horn
appellations.summary: The Horn, shared by Nieder- and Ober-Ingelheim, gives fine Pinot Noir on limestone, notably from J. Neus.
appellations.terroir: About 21 ha of limestone and loess. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bingen and the Grosslage Kaiserpfalz (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 21.4 ha are registered under vine.

appellations.name: Büdesheimer Scharlachberg
appellations.summary: The Scharlachberg ('scarlet hill') at Bingen-Büdesheim owes its name to red quartzite and slate soils. It is the best-known site of Bingen, giving spicy, mineral Riesling.
appellations.terroir: About 26 ha of quartzite and red slate on steep south-facing slopes above the Nahe and Rhine, geologically close to the Rheingau's Rüdesheimer Berg. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Bingen and the Grosslage St.  Rochuskapelle (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 25.6 ha are registered under vine.

appellations.name: Bechtheimer Geyersberg
appellations.summary: A Bechtheim site of about 79 ha on limestone and loess, giving full, ripe Riesling and Pinot.
appellations.terroir: Limestone, loess and marl. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Wonnegau and the Grosslage Pilgerpfad (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 79.1 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Bechtheim include Hasensprung.

appellations.name: Bechtheimer Hasensprung
appellations.summary: A large Bechtheim site of about 174 ha on loess and limestone, giving ripe white and red wines.
appellations.terroir: Loess over limestone. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Wonnegau and the Grosslage Pilgerpfad (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 173.5 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Bechtheim include Geyersberg.

appellations.name: Forster Kirchenstück
appellations.summary: The Kirchenstück is a walled, almost flat vineyard of about 3.6 ha behind the church in Forst, and by price and reputation the greatest site of the Pfalz. Its Rieslings are not loud but complete: silky, multilayered, with citrus, white flowers and a long, salty finish. The Bavarian land-tax survey of the Palatinate in 1828 already valued it above every other Forst site. Bürklin-Wolf, von Buhl, Bassermann-Jordan, Mosbacher and Acham-Magin share it.
appellations.terroir: A complex mix of sandstone, limestone and basalt rubble washed down from the Pechsteinkopf, on a gentle east-facing slope at about 130 m, sheltered by the Haardt hills and the walls of the village. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Mariengarten (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 3.6 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Forst include Ungeheuer, Pechstein, Elster and Jesuitengarten.
appellations.nerd_note: Bürklin-Wolf labels its Kirchenstück 'G.C.' (grand cru) under a Burgundy-inspired estate classification it adopted in the 1990s, before the VDP built its own pyramid.

appellations.name: Forster Jesuitengarten
appellations.summary: The Jesuitengarten was a property of the Jesuits until their order was suppressed in 1773. This small, walled Forst site gives aromatic, elegant Riesling, slightly more open than the Kirchenstück. Bassermann-Jordan, von Buhl, Bürklin-Wolf and von Winning make reference wines. Forst's four grand sites, Kirchenstück, Jesuitengarten, Pechstein and Ungeheuer, lie side by side along barely two kilometres of hillside, which makes Forst the classic place to taste how basalt, limestone and sandstone change Riesling.
appellations.terroir: About 7 ha of sandy loam with basalt and limestone fragments on a gentle east-facing slope. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Mariengarten (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 6.8 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Forst include Ungeheuer, Pechstein, Elster and Freundstück.

appellations.name: Forster Pechstein
appellations.summary: The Pechstein ('pitch stone') takes its name from black basalt, the remnant of an extinct volcano, the Pechsteinkopf, above Forst. The dark stones absorb heat, and the Rieslings are smoky, spicy and taut, the most mineral of the Forst grand sites. Bürklin-Wolf, von Winning, Mosbacher and von Buhl lead.
appellations.terroir: About 16 ha of basalt rubble over sandy loam, on a gentle slope facing east. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Mariengarten (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 15.7 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Forst include Ungeheuer, Elster, Jesuitengarten and Freundstück.
appellations.nerd_note: Basalt from the Pechsteinkopf was quarried for centuries and, by local tradition, spread in neighbouring Forst vineyards to darken and warm the soil.

appellations.name: Forster Ungeheuer
appellations.summary: The Ungeheuer ('monster') is the largest of Forst's grand sites, about 33 ha. Otto von Bismarck is said to have remarked that the monster tasted very good. Its Rieslings are full, ripe and spicy, with power and grip from basalt and limestone. As the largest of the four Forst grand sites, it is also the easiest to find and often the best introduction to the village.
appellations.terroir: Basalt, limestone and sandstone rubble on gentle east-facing slopes. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Mariengarten (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 33 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Forst include Pechstein, Elster, Jesuitengarten and Freundstück.
appellations.nerd_note: The name is usually traced to a local family called Ungeheuer, not to any beast.

appellations.name: Forster Freundstück
appellations.summary: A small Forst site of about 3.5 ha next to the Kirchenstück, giving fine, mineral Riesling, notably from von Buhl.
appellations.terroir: Sandstone, limestone and basalt rubble. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Mariengarten (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 3.5 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Forst include Ungeheuer, Pechstein, Elster and Jesuitengarten.

appellations.name: Forster Elster
appellations.summary: A Forst site of about 8 ha, giving ripe, aromatic Riesling.
appellations.terroir: Sandy loam with basalt fragments. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Mariengarten (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 7.7 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Forst include Ungeheuer, Pechstein, Jesuitengarten and Freundstück.

appellations.name: Deidesheimer Hohenmorgen
appellations.summary: The Hohenmorgen is a tiny, slightly elevated site of about 2.8 ha in Deidesheim, giving a dense, deep Riesling with smoky spice. Bassermann-Jordan and Bürklin-Wolf are the main owners.
appellations.terroir: Sandstone and loam with some limestone, east facing. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Mariengarten (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 2.8 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Deidesheim include Paradiesgarten, Kieselberg, Leinhöhle and Grainhübel.

appellations.name: Deidesheimer Kalkofen
appellations.summary: The Kalkofen ('lime kiln') in Deidesheim is named after the limestone that was burned here; it gives full, firm Riesling with a chalky grip.
appellations.terroir: About 5 ha of limestone and loam. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Mariengarten (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 4.8 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Deidesheim include Paradiesgarten, Kieselberg, Leinhöhle and Grainhübel.

appellations.name: Deidesheimer Grainhübel
appellations.summary: A Deidesheim site of about 5 ha giving spicy, elegant Riesling, from Bassermann-Jordan and von Winning among others.
appellations.terroir: Sandstone, loam and limestone. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Mariengarten (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 5.3 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Deidesheim include Paradiesgarten, Kieselberg, Leinhöhle and Langenmorgen.

appellations.name: Deidesheimer Langenmorgen
appellations.summary: The Langenmorgen is a long, narrow Deidesheim site of about 10 ha where von Winning makes one of its most celebrated Grosse Gewächse: aromatic, oak-framed and long.
appellations.terroir: Sandy loam over sandstone on a gentle slope below the Haardt forest. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Mariengarten (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 9.8 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Deidesheim include Paradiesgarten, Kieselberg, Leinhöhle and Grainhübel.

appellations.name: Deidesheimer Leinhöhle
appellations.summary: A Deidesheim site of about 18 ha, giving juicy, fragrant Riesling from Bassermann-Jordan, von Winning and others.
appellations.terroir: Sandy loam and sandstone rubble. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Mariengarten (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 17.9 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Deidesheim include Paradiesgarten, Kieselberg, Grainhübel and Langenmorgen.

appellations.name: Deidesheimer Kieselberg
appellations.summary: A Deidesheim site of about 16 ha with pebbly soils, giving fresh, elegant Riesling.
appellations.terroir: Sand, gravel and pebbles ('Kiesel'). In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Mariengarten (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 15.7 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Deidesheim include Paradiesgarten, Leinhöhle, Grainhübel and Langenmorgen.

appellations.name: Deidesheimer Paradiesgarten
appellations.summary: A Deidesheim site of about 30 ha at the forest edge, giving fresh Riesling and Pinot.
appellations.terroir: Sandstone and loam, higher and cooler. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Mariengarten (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 30.2 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Deidesheim include Kieselberg, Leinhöhle, Grainhübel and Langenmorgen.

appellations.name: Ruppertsberger Gaisböhl
appellations.summary: The Gaisböhl is a walled monopole of Dr. Bürklin-Wolf in Ruppertsberg, giving a firm, citrus-driven Riesling that Bürklin-Wolf ranks as a grand cru.
appellations.terroir: Sandy loam with sandstone and some basalt. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Hofstück (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages). Neighbouring sites in Ruppertsberg include Reiterpfad, Hoheburg and Spiess.

appellations.name: Ruppertsberger Reiterpfad
appellations.summary: A large Ruppertsberg site of about 77 ha whose best parcels give rich, aromatic Riesling, notably from von Buhl, Christmann and Bassermann-Jordan.
appellations.terroir: Sand, loam and limestone. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Hofstück (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 77.4 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Ruppertsberg include Hoheburg, Gaisböhl and Spiess.

appellations.name: Ruppertsberger Spiess
appellations.summary: A small Ruppertsberg site of about 5.5 ha giving fine, mineral Riesling, from von Buhl and Bürklin-Wolf.
appellations.terroir: Sandy loam and sandstone. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Hofstück (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 5.5 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Ruppertsberg include Reiterpfad, Hoheburg and Gaisböhl.

appellations.name: Ruppertsberger Hoheburg
appellations.summary: A Ruppertsberg site of about 18 ha giving fruity, approachable Riesling, notably from Bürklin-Wolf.
appellations.terroir: Sandy loam over gravel. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Hofstück (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 18.4 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Ruppertsberg include Reiterpfad, Gaisböhl and Spiess.

appellations.name: Wachenheimer Gerümpel
appellations.summary: The Gerümpel is Wachenheim's most famous site, giving vibrant, precise Riesling from Bürklin-Wolf, Karl Schaefer and others.
appellations.terroir: About 13 ha of sandstone, sand and loam on a gentle east-facing slope. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Mariengarten (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 12.8 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Wachenheim include Böhlig, Goldbächel, Belz and Rechbächel.

appellations.name: Wachenheimer Goldbächel
appellations.summary: A small Wachenheim site of about 4 ha giving lively, mineral Riesling.
appellations.terroir: Sandstone and loam. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Mariengarten (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 4 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Wachenheim include Böhlig, Gerümpel, Belz and Rechbächel.

appellations.name: Wachenheimer Rechbächel
appellations.summary: A small walled Wachenheim site, a monopole of Bürklin-Wolf, giving fine, fragrant Riesling.
appellations.terroir: Sandstone and loam behind walls. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Mariengarten (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages). Neighbouring sites in Wachenheim include Böhlig, Gerümpel, Goldbächel and Belz.

appellations.name: Wachenheimer Böhlig
appellations.summary: A Wachenheim site of about 5.5 ha giving firm, spicy Riesling, for example from Bürklin-Wolf.
appellations.terroir: Sandstone, loam and limestone. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Mariengarten (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 5.5 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Wachenheim include Gerümpel, Goldbächel, Belz and Rechbächel.

appellations.name: Wachenheimer Belz
appellations.summary: A small Wachenheim site at the forest edge, giving cool, elegant Riesling.
appellations.terroir: Sandstone and loam on a higher slope. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Mariengarten (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages). Neighbouring sites in Wachenheim include Böhlig, Gerümpel, Goldbächel and Rechbächel.

appellations.name: Königsbacher Idig
appellations.summary: The Idig is a limestone site at Königsbach near Neustadt that Steffen Christmann made into one of the leading Grosse Gewächse of the Pfalz, both for Riesling and Pinot Noir. The Riesling is powerful, chalky and long. Christmann converted to biodynamic farming in the 2000s, and Steffen Christmann served for many years as president of the VDP, shaping its classification of Grosse Lagen.
appellations.terroir: About 16 ha of limestone and marl with some sandstone rubble on a south-east-facing slope. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Meerspinne (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 16.4 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Königsbach include Ölberg.

appellations.name: Königsbacher Ölberg
appellations.summary: A Königsbach site of about 28 ha giving ripe, mineral Riesling, notably from Christmann.
appellations.terroir: Limestone and sandstone. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Meerspinne (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 28.5 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Königsbach include Idig.

appellations.name: Mandelgarten
appellations.summary: The Mandelgarten, shared by Gimmeldingen and Mussbach, is lined with almond trees that blossom in March, the first sign of spring along the German Wine Route. Christmann makes an elegant, floral Riesling here.
appellations.terroir: About 26 ha of sandy loam and sandstone. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Meerspinne (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 25.7 ha are registered under vine.

appellations.name: Haardter Herrenletten
appellations.summary: A Haardt site of about 15 ha near Neustadt, giving full, aromatic Riesling and Rieslaner from Müller-Catoir.
appellations.terroir: Loam and clay ('Letten') on a gentle slope. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Meerspinne (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 14.9 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Haardt include Bürgergarten.

appellations.name: Haardter Bürgergarten
appellations.summary: The Bürgergarten at Haardt includes the parcel 'im Breumel', the source of Müller-Catoir's Grosses Gewächs: aromatic, floral and filigree Riesling.
appellations.terroir: About 18 ha of sandstone and loam at the foot of the Haardt hills. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Meerspinne (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 18.4 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Haardt include Herrenletten.

appellations.name: Kallstadter Saumagen
appellations.summary: The Saumagen is a former Roman limestone quarry above Kallstadt, named after its shape like a pig's stomach (also a Palatinate dish). Koehler-Ruprecht's Rieslings from here, made in an old-fashioned way in large casks, are legendary for their longevity. The wines are powerful and chalky, with a salty finish.
appellations.terroir: About 40 ha of limestone and marl on a south-east-facing slope, very warm and dry. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Kobnert (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 39.8 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Kallstadt include Steinacker.
appellations.nerd_note: Kallstadt is also the ancestral village of the Trump and Heinz families, a coincidence locals mention with mixed feelings.

appellations.name: Kallstadter Steinacker
appellations.summary: A large Kallstadt site of about 123 ha on limestone, giving rich Riesling and Pinot, with some top parcels.
appellations.terroir: Limestone and loam. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Kobnert (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 122.6 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Kallstadt include Saumagen.

appellations.name: Ungsteiner Weilberg
appellations.summary: The Weilberg at Ungstein is named after a Roman villa (villa rustica) excavated in the vineyard, complete with a Roman wine press. It gives spicy, intense Riesling on limestone and red soils, notably from Pfeffingen and Rings. The excavated Roman estate, with its wine-pressing basins, is open to visitors among the vines and shows that grapes were pressed here about 1,700 years ago.
appellations.terroir: About 33 ha of limestone with red, iron-rich clay (terra rossa) on a south-east slope. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Honigsäckel (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 32.8 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Ungstein include Herrenberg.

appellations.name: Ungsteiner Herrenberg
appellations.summary: A Ungstein site of about 29 ha giving juicy, aromatic Riesling, from Pfeffingen and others.
appellations.terroir: Limestone and loam. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Honigsäckel (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 28.6 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Ungstein include Weilberg.

appellations.name: Michelsberg
appellations.summary: The Michelsberg rises above Bad Dürkheim next to the ruins of a chapel of St. Michael, site of the town's famous wine fair (the Wurstmarkt) since the Middle Ages. It gives ripe, aromatic Riesling.
appellations.terroir: About 8 ha of limestone and sandstone. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Hochmess (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 7.7 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Bad Dürkheim include Spielberg.

appellations.name: Dürkheimer Spielberg
appellations.summary: A Bad Dürkheim site of about 14 ha on limestone, giving firm Riesling and fine Pinot Noir from Rings and Karl Schaefer.
appellations.terroir: Limestone and loam. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Hochmess (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 14.1 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Bad Dürkheim include Michelsberg.

appellations.name: Laumersheimer Kirschgarten
appellations.summary: The Kirschgarten at Laumersheim is one of the best Pinot Noir sites in Germany, made famous by Knipser and Philipp Kuhn. The wines are deep, structured and age-worthy. Werner and Volker Knipser were among the first in Germany to age Pinot Noir in new barriques in the 1980s, and the northern Pfalz limestone proved ideal for it.
appellations.terroir: About 47 ha of limestone and marl, south facing, at the northern end of the Pfalz. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Schwarzerde (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 47.3 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Laumersheim include Steinbuckel.

appellations.name: Laumersheimer Steinbuckel
appellations.summary: A Laumersheim site of about 62 ha on limestone where Philipp Kuhn and Knipser grow Riesling and Pinot.
appellations.terroir: Limestone and loess. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Schwarzerde (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 62.4 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Laumersheim include Kirschgarten.

appellations.name: Großkarlbacher Burgweg
appellations.summary: A large Grosskarlbach site whose best parcels give dense Riesling and Pinot Noir from Knipser and Philipp Kuhn.
appellations.terroir: Limestone and loess. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Mittelhaardt/Dt. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Schwarzerde (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 128.1 ha are registered under vine.

appellations.name: Birkweilerer Kastanienbusch
appellations.summary: The Kastanienbusch ('chestnut grove') at Birkweiler is the great site of the southern Pfalz, rising to over 300 m at the edge of the Palatinate Forest. Its unusual red soils from Rotliegend, plus granite and slate, give Rieslings of spice, power and length; the steep 'Köppel' parcel is the core. Dr. Wehrheim, Ökonomierat Rebholz, Siegrist and Gies-Düppel make the reference wines.
appellations.terroir: About 67 ha registered, with red Rotliegend sandstone, weathered granite and slate on steep, south-east-facing slopes; chestnut woods surround the vines and cool nights keep acidity bright. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Südl. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Königsgarten (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 67.5 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Birkweiler include Mandelberg.
appellations.nerd_note: Few places in Germany show such a jumble of rocks within one slope; growers bottle the Köppel separately because of its red stony soil.

appellations.name: Birkweilerer Mandelberg
appellations.summary: The Mandelberg at Birkweiler is a limestone site famous for Pinot Blanc and Pinot Gris, especially Dr. Wehrheim's Weissburgunder Grosses Gewächs.
appellations.terroir: About 27 ha of limestone (Muschelkalk) and marl. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Südl. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Königsgarten (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 26.8 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Birkweiler include Kastanienbusch.

appellations.name: Siebeldingener Im Sonnenschein
appellations.summary: Im Sonnenschein ('in the sunshine') at Siebeldingen is the flagship of Ökonomierat Rebholz, whose dry Riesling, Pinot Blanc and Pinot Noir from here are taut and long-lived.
appellations.terroir: About 97 ha registered, shell limestone and loam on south-facing slopes. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Südl. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Königsgarten (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 97.1 ha are registered under vine.

appellations.name: Godramsteiner Münzberg
appellations.summary: A very large Godramstein site of about 430 ha, whose name was taken by Weingut Münzberg, known for Pinot.
appellations.terroir: Loess, limestone and loam. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Südl. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Königsgarten (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 433.5 ha are registered under vine.

appellations.name: Burrweilerer Schäwer
appellations.summary: The Schäwer at Burrweiler is the only slate site of the Pfalz, a small outcrop of the same kind of rock as the Mosel. Herbert Messmer's Rieslings from it are cool, fine and slatey.
appellations.terroir: About 23 ha registered, with Devonian slate on the slopes of the Haardt. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Südl. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Bischofskreuz (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 23.2 ha are registered under vine.
appellations.nerd_note: The name comes from the dialect word for slate ('Schiefer').

appellations.name: Gleisweilerer Hölle
appellations.summary: A Gleisweiler site of about 58 ha in a warm hollow, giving ripe Riesling and Pinot from Minges and others.
appellations.terroir: Sandstone, loam and limestone. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Südl. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Bischofskreuz (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 57.6 ha are registered under vine.

appellations.name: Sonnenberg
appellations.summary: A large site shared by Ilbesheim and Leinsweiler, giving fresh Riesling and Pinot, with Siegrist among the best growers.
appellations.terroir: Limestone, loess and sandstone. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Südl. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Herrlich (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 120 ha are registered under vine.

appellations.name: Kalmit
appellations.summary: The Kalmit, shared by Arzheim and Ilbesheim, is a limestone hill where Kranz makes one of the most admired Rieslings of the southern Pfalz.
appellations.terroir: About 94 ha of shell limestone and marl on south-facing slopes. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Südl. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Herrlich (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 93.8 ha are registered under vine.

appellations.name: Sonnenberg
appellations.summary: The Sonnenberg runs across the French border at Schweigen: many of its vines lie in Alsace near Wissembourg but, under a long-standing cross-border arrangement, their grapes are made into German wine. Friedrich Becker and Bernhart make outstanding Pinot Noir here, with Becker's parcel wines (Kammerberg, Sankt Paul) among the best German reds. The best parcels lie on limestone ridges that continue south into Alsace.
appellations.terroir: About 276 ha registered, with limestone and marl in the best parcels and loess elsewhere. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Südl. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Guttenberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 276.4 ha are registered under vine.
appellations.nerd_note: Becker's Kammerberg parcel lies on French soil, which once forced the estate to label it without the site name.

appellations.name: Frankweilerer Kalkgrube
appellations.summary: A Frankweiler site of about 96 ha on limestone, giving fresh white wines and Pinot.
appellations.terroir: Limestone and loess. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Südl. Weinstraße and the Grosslage Königsgarten (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 95.6 ha are registered under vine.

appellations.name: Ahrweilerer Kräuterberg
appellations.summary: The Kräuterberg ('herb hill') at Walporzheim is the Ahr's most legendary slope, a narrow amphitheatre of terraces held up by slate walls, so steep and hot that wild herbs grow between the vines. Its Pinot Noirs are dark, spicy and concentrated, with a cool slate finish. Meyer-Näkel and Jean Stodden have helped restore its terraces, several of which had been abandoned. The catastrophic flood of 14 July 2021 devastated the valley's villages and cellars; the steep vineyards themselves mostly survived.
appellations.terroir: About 5 ha of Devonian slate and greywacke terraces facing south and south-west; the walls and rock store heat in a valley that is otherwise one of Germany's northernmost red-wine areas. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Walporzheim/Ahrtal and the Grosslage Klosterberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 5.1 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Ahrweiler include Rosenthal, Silberberg and Gärkammer.
appellations.nerd_note: The legal label calls it Ahrweilerer Kräuterberg because Walporzheim belongs to Bad Neuenahr-Ahrweiler, but growers still use the historic name Walporzheimer Kräuterberg.

appellations.name: Ahrweilerer Gärkammer
appellations.summary: The Gärkammer is a tiny walled slope of about 0.7 ha at Walporzheim, the monopole of J. J. Adeneuer, giving dense, smoky Pinot Noir.
appellations.terroir: Slate and greywacke in a sheltered hollow. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Walporzheim/Ahrtal and the Grosslage Klosterberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages). Neighbouring sites in Ahrweiler include Rosenthal, Silberberg and Kräuterberg.

appellations.name: Ahrweilerer Rosenthal
appellations.summary: The Rosenthal is a sheltered, south-facing Ahrweiler site where loess and loam over slate give rounder, fleshier Pinot Noir than the bare slopes upstream. J. J. Adeneuer and Meyer-Näkel bottle it.
appellations.terroir: About 21 ha of loess and loam over slate and greywacke. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Walporzheim/Ahrtal and the Grosslage Klosterberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 21 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Ahrweiler include Silberberg, Gärkammer and Kräuterberg.

appellations.name: Ahrweilerer Silberberg
appellations.summary: A steep Ahrweiler site of about 14 ha on slate, giving firm, fine Pinot Noir from Meyer-Näkel and others.
appellations.terroir: Slate and greywacke with quartzite. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Walporzheim/Ahrtal and the Grosslage Klosterberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 14 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Ahrweiler include Rosenthal, Gärkammer and Kräuterberg.

appellations.name: Dernauer Pfarrwingert
appellations.summary: The Pfarrwingert ('parish vineyard') at Dernau is a steep slope of slate whose Pinot Noirs, especially from Meyer-Näkel, are fine-boned, perfumed and long.
appellations.terroir: About 9 ha of Devonian slate and greywacke on a south-facing slope. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Walporzheim/Ahrtal and the Grosslage Klosterberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 8.8 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Dernau include Hardtberg.

appellations.name: Dernauer Hardtberg
appellations.summary: A Dernau site of about 24 ha on slate, giving cool, finely spiced Pinot Noir, for Meyer-Näkel and Kreuzberg.
appellations.terroir: Slate and greywacke, steep and terraced in parts. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Walporzheim/Ahrtal and the Grosslage Klosterberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 24 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Dernau include Pfarrwingert.

appellations.name: Mayschoßer Mönchberg
appellations.summary: The Mönchberg at Mayschoss is a steep slate slope once owned by monks, giving elegant Pinot Noir. Deutzerhof and the Mayschoss cooperative, founded in 1868 and the oldest wine cooperative in Germany, work here.
appellations.terroir: About 60 ha of slate and greywacke on steep slopes above a loop of the Ahr. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Walporzheim/Ahrtal and the Grosslage Klosterberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 60.4 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Mayschoß include Laacherberg.

appellations.name: Mayschoßer Laacherberg
appellations.summary: A steep Mayschoss site of about 15 ha named after Maria Laach abbey, which owned vineyards here, giving spicy Pinot Noir.
appellations.terroir: Slate and greywacke. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Walporzheim/Ahrtal and the Grosslage Klosterberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 15.3 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Mayschoß include Mönchberg.

appellations.name: Altenahrer Eck
appellations.summary: The Eck at Altenahr is the uppermost great site of the Ahr, a steep, rocky slope at a bend of the river where Deutzerhof and Jean Stodden make taut, mineral Pinot Noir.
appellations.terroir: About 10 ha of slate and greywacke, very steep, south facing. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Walporzheim/Ahrtal and the Grosslage Klosterberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 9.6 ha are registered under vine.

appellations.name: Neuenahrer Sonnenberg
appellations.summary: A Bad Neuenahr site of about 24 ha with loess and slate, giving supple Pinot Noir, notably from J. J. Adeneuer and Jean Stodden.
appellations.terroir: Loess and loam over slate. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Walporzheim/Ahrtal and the Grosslage Klosterberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 23.7 ha are registered under vine.

appellations.name: Burggarten
appellations.summary: A lower Ahr site of about 14 ha at Heimersheim with loess soils, giving softer, fruity Pinot Noir.
appellations.terroir: Loess and loam near the mouth of the valley. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Walporzheim/Ahrtal and the Grosslage Klosterberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 14.4 ha are registered under vine.

appellations.name: Recher Herrenberg
appellations.summary: A Rech site of about 18 ha on slate, giving fine Pinot Noir and some Riesling, close to the old stone bridge of Rech.
appellations.terroir: Slate and greywacke slopes. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Walporzheim/Ahrtal and the Grosslage Klosterberg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 17.8 ha are registered under vine.

appellations.name: Bopparder Feuerlay
appellations.summary: The Feuerlay ('fire rock') is the best-known section of the Bopparder Hamm, the great loop of the Rhine at Boppard where the river turns through 180 degrees and the slope faces full south. Matthias Müller's Rieslings from here are fine, spicy and long, with a cool slate finish.
appellations.terroir: About 17 ha of Devonian slate on steep south-facing slopes at the apex of the bend; the wide river reflects light, and the deep gorge shelters the vines from cold winds. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Loreley and the Grosslage Gedeonseck (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 16.7 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Boppard include Engelstein, Mandelstein and Ohlenberg.
appellations.nerd_note: The Bopparder Hamm is divided into several Einzellagen (Feuerlay, Mandelstein, Ohlenberg, Engelstein, Fässerlay, Elfenlay, Weingrube); the whole loop sits inside the Upper Middle Rhine Valley UNESCO World Heritage Site.

appellations.name: Bopparder Mandelstein
appellations.summary: A steep section of the Bopparder Hamm, about 11 ha, giving ripe, mineral Riesling from Matthias Müller and others.
appellations.terroir: Slate, south-facing. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Loreley and the Grosslage Gedeonseck (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 10.7 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Boppard include Feuerlay, Engelstein and Ohlenberg.

appellations.name: Bopparder Ohlenberg
appellations.summary: A section of the Bopparder Hamm of about 8 ha, giving firm, slatey Riesling.
appellations.terroir: Devonian slate on a steep slope. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Loreley and the Grosslage Gedeonseck (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 8.1 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Boppard include Feuerlay, Engelstein and Mandelstein.

appellations.name: Engelstein
appellations.summary: A small section of the Bopparder Hamm shared with Spay, giving fine, fragrant Riesling.
appellations.terroir: Slate on the downstream arm of the loop. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Loreley and the Grosslage Gedeonseck (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 3.8 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Boppard include Feuerlay, Mandelstein and Ohlenberg.

appellations.name: Bacharacher Hahn
appellations.summary: The Hahn is a steep, south-facing slope of slate just upstream of Bacharach, the monopole of Toni Jost. Its Rieslings are taut and racy, with a smoky slate finish, and Jost also makes sweet wines of great purity here. In the Middle Ages Bacharach was the shipping port for Rhine wine, which was sold far and wide as 'Bacharacher'; the town walls and towers still run along the vineyard edge.
appellations.terroir: About 5 ha of grey Devonian slate rising directly from the Rhine. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Loreley and the Grosslage Schloß Stahleck (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 5 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Bacharach include Wolfshöhle, Posten and St. Jost.

appellations.name: Bacharacher Posten
appellations.summary: The Posten lies right behind the town walls of Bacharach, a steep slope of slate where Ratzenberger and Bastian make fine, aromatic Riesling.
appellations.terroir: About 5 ha of slate on a south-east-facing slope above the old town. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Loreley and the Grosslage Schloß Stahleck (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 4.8 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Bacharach include Wolfshöhle, Hahn and St. Jost.

appellations.name: Bacharacher Wolfshöhle
appellations.summary: A steep Bacharach site of about 22 ha whose slate gives cool, firm Riesling, notably from Ratzenberger.
appellations.terroir: Slate on the slopes around the Steeg valley. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Loreley and the Grosslage Schloß Stahleck (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 21.9 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Bacharach include Hahn, Posten and St. Jost.

appellations.name: St. Jost
appellations.summary: St. Jost in the Steeg side valley above Bacharach is a steep slate site named after a chapel of St. Jodocus. Ratzenberger's Rieslings and sparkling wines from here are taut and elegant.
appellations.terroir: About 7 ha of slate in a cooler side valley. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Loreley and the Grosslage Schloß Stahleck (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 6.7 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Bacharach include Wolfshöhle, Hahn and Posten.

appellations.name: Oberweseler Ölsberg
appellations.summary: The Ölsberg is a steep slope of slate on the right bank opposite Oberwesel, a small, terraced site giving dense, mineral Riesling.
appellations.terroir: About 6 ha of slate terraces facing south-west across the Rhine. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Loreley and the Grosslage Schloß Schönburg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 5.9 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Oberwesel include Bernstein.

appellations.name: Oberweseler Bernstein
appellations.summary: The Bernstein lies in the Engehöll side valley near Oberwesel, an old terraced site that Lanius-Knab bottles as Engehöller Bernstein: cool, perfumed Riesling with racy acidity.
appellations.terroir: About 11 ha of slate on steep terraces. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Loreley and the Grosslage Schloß Schönburg (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 10.6 ha are registered under vine. Neighbouring sites in Oberwesel include Ölsberg.

appellations.name: Oberdiebacher Fürstenberg
appellations.summary: A steep Oberdiebach site of about 21 ha below the Fürstenberg castle ruin, giving fine, aromatic Riesling.
appellations.terroir: Slate on a steep slope in the Diebach valley. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Loreley and the Grosslage Schloß Stahleck (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 21.2 ha are registered under vine.

appellations.name: Leutesdorfer Gartenlay
appellations.summary: A Leutesdorf site of about 45 ha on the lower Middle Rhine, giving lively Riesling and some Pinot Noir.
appellations.terroir: Slate and loess on south-facing slopes. In the Rhineland-Palatinate vineyard register (Weinbergsrolle) it sits in the Bereich Loreley and the Grosslage Burg Hammerstein (a 1971 collective name for blends from several villages); about 44.8 ha are registered under vine.

appellations.name: Ried Achleiten
appellations.summary: The Achleiten is the great hill of Weißenkirchen and Joching, a bulging promontory of terraces that rises from the Danube at the downstream end of the village. It is one of the most complex sites of the Wachau, and its Rieslings and Grüner Veltliners combine ripe stone fruit with a smoky, salty, almost flinty minerality that tasters recognise blind.
