Prager (where Toni Bodenstein studied the site's geology in detail), Domäne Wachau, Rudi Pichler and Holzapfel make reference Smaragd wines.
appellations.terroir: About 22 ha of dry-stone terraces between roughly 200 and 360 m, facing south and south-west. The lower slope is mica schist and paragneiss; higher up come gneiss and dark amphibolite, with patches of loess and marble (metamorphosed limestone). Topsoil is thin, so the vines root into the rock. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Weißenkirchen (municipality Weißenkirchen in der Wachau), with about 20 ha delimited. Named subrieden: Himmelreich.
appellations.nerd_note: Bodenstein has pointed to bands of amphibolite and serpentinite running through the hill and links these magnesium-rich rocks to the wines' salty edge; the subried Achleiten Himmelreich is the uppermost part.

appellations.name: Ried Klaus
appellations.summary: The Klaus is a steep, narrow terraced site between Weißenkirchen and Joching that Josef Jamek made famous: his Riesling Ried Klaus of the late 1950s is often cited as the first great dry single-vineyard Riesling of the Wachau, at a time when most Austrian wine was sweetened. Today Prager, Jamek and others make taut, mineral Riesling here. The narrow terraces are among the steepest of Weißenkirchen and can only be worked by hand.
appellations.terroir: About 15 to 20 ha of gneiss and amphibolite terraces facing south-east, sheltered by the Achleiten hill. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Weißenkirchen (municipality Weißenkirchen in der Wachau), with about 20 ha delimited.
appellations.nerd_note: Jamek's family inn in Joching, run for more than a century, was where many visitors first tasted dry Wachau Riesling.

appellations.name: Ried Steinriegl
appellations.summary: The Steinriegl ('stone ridge') climbs high behind Weißenkirchen, one of the coolest top sites of the village thanks to its altitude and the winds that drop out of the Waldviertel forest at night. Prager and Domäne Wachau make sleek, perfumed Riesling here.
appellations.terroir: Terraces of gneiss and mica schist rising to over 400 m, south-facing; cooler nights than the river-side sites. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Weißenkirchen (municipality Weißenkirchen in der Wachau), with about 30 ha delimited. Named subrieden: Lichtgartl.

appellations.name: Ried Steinriegl
appellations.summary: The Steinriegl ('stone ridge') climbs high behind Weißenkirchen, one of the coolest top sites of the village thanks to its altitude and the winds that drop out of the Waldviertel forest at night. Prager and Domäne Wachau make sleek, perfumed Riesling here. Its height has made it one of the Wachau's winners as summers have grown warmer: the wines keep their freshness in vintages when the river-side sites turn heavy.
appellations.terroir: Terraces of gneiss and mica schist rising to over 400 m, south-facing; cooler nights than the river-side sites. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Joching (municipality Weißenkirchen in der Wachau).

appellations.name: Ried Hochrain
appellations.summary: The Hochrain above Wösendorf gives some of the Wachau's most elegant Grüner Veltliner and Riesling, notably from Rudi Pichler and Franz Hirtzberger. Loess on the lower terraces softens the wines, gneiss above sharpens them. Rudi Pichler, whose winery stands in Wösendorf, ferments with natural yeasts and gives his wines long lees contact; his Hochrain Grüner Veltliner Smaragd is one of the region's most age-worthy.
appellations.terroir: Terraces of gneiss and paragneiss with loess pockets, facing south-east. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Wösendorf (municipality Weißenkirchen in der Wachau), with about 20 ha delimited. Named subrieden: Ralais.

appellations.name: Ried Kollmitz
appellations.summary: A small Ried between Joching and Wösendorf, giving fine, aromatic Grüner Veltliner and Riesling.
appellations.nerd_note: Under Wachau DAC rules (from the 2020 vintage) a Ried name may only appear on hand-harvested wines, while the Vinea Wachau terms Steinfeder, Federspiel and Smaragd still signal rising ripeness.
appellations.terroir: Gneiss and loess terraces. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Joching (municipality Weißenkirchen in der Wachau), with about 20 ha delimited.

appellations.name: Ried Kollmitz
appellations.summary: A small Ried between Joching and Wösendorf, giving fine, aromatic Grüner Veltliner and Riesling.
appellations.nerd_note: Under Wachau DAC rules (from the 2020 vintage) a Ried name may only appear on hand-harvested wines, while the Vinea Wachau terms Steinfeder, Federspiel and Smaragd still signal rising ripeness.
appellations.terroir: Gneiss and loess terraces. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Wösendorf (municipality Weißenkirchen in der Wachau).

appellations.name: Ried Kollmütz
appellations.summary: The Kollmütz behind Wösendorf is known above all for Rudi Pichler's Grüner Veltliner Smaragd, a dense, peppery wine from loess-rich terraces.
appellations.terroir: Loess over gneiss on south-facing terraces, with cool air from the side valley. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Wösendorf (municipality Weißenkirchen in der Wachau), with about 50 ha delimited.

appellations.name: Ried Ritzling
appellations.summary: A Weißenkirchen Ried on the slopes behind the village, giving fresh, mineral Riesling and Grüner Veltliner.
appellations.nerd_note: Under Wachau DAC rules (from the 2020 vintage) a Ried name may only appear on hand-harvested wines, while the Vinea Wachau terms Steinfeder, Federspiel and Smaragd still signal rising ripeness.
appellations.terroir: Gneiss terraces. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Weißenkirchen (municipality Weißenkirchen in der Wachau), with about 10 ha delimited.

appellations.name: Ried Pichl Point
appellations.summary: A Joching Ried on gentler slopes near the Danube, giving round, spicy Grüner Veltliner.
appellations.terroir: Loess and sand over gneiss. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Joching (municipality Weißenkirchen in der Wachau), with about 10 ha delimited. Named subrieden: Pichl.

appellations.name: Ried Vorderseiber
appellations.summary: The Vorderseiber is the lower, warmer part of the Seiber hill behind Weißenkirchen, giving full Grüner Veltliner on loess-rich terraces.
appellations.terroir: Loess and gneiss. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Weißenkirchen (municipality Weißenkirchen in der Wachau), with about 40 ha delimited.

appellations.name: Ried Seiberberg
appellations.summary: The Seiberberg rises high behind Weißenkirchen, a cool site whose Riesling and Grüner Veltliner are taut and perfumed.
appellations.terroir: Gneiss terraces at around 400 m, among the higher Wachau sites. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Weißenkirchen (municipality Weißenkirchen in der Wachau), with about 30 ha delimited. Named subrieden: Hochseiber.

appellations.name: Ried Buschenberg
appellations.summary: A Weißenkirchen Ried giving fine, mineral Riesling and Grüner Veltliner from terraces above the village.
appellations.nerd_note: Under Wachau DAC rules (from the 2020 vintage) a Ried name may only appear on hand-harvested wines, while the Vinea Wachau terms Steinfeder, Federspiel and Smaragd still signal rising ripeness.
appellations.terroir: Gneiss and mica schist. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Weißenkirchen (municipality Weißenkirchen in der Wachau), with about 20 ha delimited.

appellations.name: Ried Hinter der Burg
appellations.summary: Hinter der Burg ('behind the castle') is a Weißenkirchen site best known for Prager's crisp Grüner Veltliner Federspiel.
appellations.terroir: Loess and gneiss on lower terraces. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Weißenkirchen (municipality Weißenkirchen in der Wachau), with about 10 ha delimited.

appellations.summary: A Wösendorf Ried on steep terraces, giving fine Riesling and Grüner Veltliner (not to be confused with the Kamptal's Gaisberg).

appellations.terroir: Gneiss and amphibolite. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Joching (municipality Weißenkirchen in der Wachau), with about 30 ha delimited. Named subrieden: Postaller.

appellations.name: Ried Kellerberg
appellations.summary: The Kellerberg is a steep, terraced slope just west of Dürnstein, and the source of some of the most powerful dry Rieslings and Grüner Veltliners of the Wachau. F.X. Pichler's Kellerberg Smaragds, with their mix of opulence, smoke and cool minerality, made the site famous in the 1990s; Knoll and Domäne Wachau also own parcels. A side valley feeds cool air into the vineyard at night, which keeps aromas fresh despite the heat of the terraces.
appellations.terroir: About 15 ha of terraces between about 220 and 400 m, with sandy loess over primary rock of gneiss and quartz. The subrieden Wunderburg and Küss den Pfennig are named on the official map. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Dürnstein, with about 20 ha delimited.
appellations.nerd_note: The site sits where a side valley opens behind Dürnstein; the night-time downdraught is the Kellerberg's secret, keeping very ripe wines fresh.

appellations.name: Ried Loibenberg
appellations.summary: The Loibenberg is the great sun-trap of Loiben, a broad, steep amphitheatre of terraces above Unterloiben facing full south. Its wines are ripe, rich and spicy, with Riesling showing apricot and Grüner Veltliner tobacco and pepper. Knoll, F.X. Pichler, Leo Alzinger and Tegernseerhof are reference growers. Some growers now worry that in hot summers it can become too warm, which is why cooler sites are gaining favour.
appellations.terroir: About 40 ha registered, gneiss and paragneiss with loess on the lower parts; subrieden include Süssenberg, Rothenberg, Langen Zung and Rauheneck. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Unterloiben (municipality Dürnstein), with about 40 ha delimited.
appellations.nerd_note: The Loibenberg is the Wachau's warmest large site because the valley opens towards the Pannonian east here.

appellations.name: Ried Schütt
appellations.summary: The Schütt is a site of alluvial gravel and sand washed down from a side valley between Dürnstein and Loiben. Knoll's Riesling Smaragd Schütt is one of the Wachau's classics, broad and juicy with a peppery bite. Because the soils are deep and loose, vines root easily and could crop heavily, so growers keep yields small; Knoll's Schütt Rieslings are famous for ageing two decades and more.
appellations.terroir: Gravel, sand and gneiss debris on a gentle fan at the foot of the hills. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Dürnstein.
appellations.nerd_note: 'Schütt' means debris or rubble, describing the material the side valley dumps onto the slope.

appellations.name: Ried Schütt
appellations.summary: The Schütt is a site of alluvial gravel and sand washed down from a side valley between Dürnstein and Loiben. Knoll's Riesling Smaragd Schütt is one of the Wachau's classics, broad and juicy with a peppery bite.
appellations.terroir: Gravel, sand and gneiss debris on a gentle fan at the foot of the hills. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Unterloiben (municipality Dürnstein).
appellations.nerd_note: 'Schütt' means debris or rubble, describing the material the side valley dumps onto the slope.

appellations.name: Ried Steinertal
appellations.summary: The Steinertal is a narrow, steep side valley above Loiben where cool air drains down at night. Its Rieslings, especially from Leo Alzinger and F.X. Pichler, are among the most delicate and crystalline of the Wachau. Cool air drains down the valley from the Waldviertel plateau at night, so night temperatures are lower here than on the Loibenberg next door, and Alzinger's Steinertal Riesling is often the most perfumed wine of the estate.
appellations.terroir: Gneiss terraces in a cool, north-south side valley. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Unterloiben (municipality Dürnstein), with about 10 ha delimited.

appellations.name: Ried Höhereck

appellations.terroir: Gneiss terraces at altitude. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Dürnstein, with about 10 ha delimited.

appellations.name: Ried Singerriedel
appellations.summary: The Singerriedel is the steep amphitheatre of terraces directly behind Spitz, rising above the church. Franz Hirtzberger's Riesling Smaragd from here is one of Austria's iconic white wines, aromatic and silky with a cool, stony core. The site is cooler than the Loibenberg because Spitz sits at the upstream end of the Wachau, where the valley narrows and air from the Waldviertel flows down at night.
appellations.terroir: Gneiss and paragneiss terraces from the village up to around 450 m, south to south-east facing, with very thin topsoil. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Spitz, with about 10 ha delimited.
appellations.nerd_note: Spitz is the last wine village of the Wachau's north bank before the valley turns into the cool Spitzer Graben, which is why its wines are finer-boned than Loiben's.

appellations.name: Ried 1000-Eimerberg
appellations.summary: The Tausendeimerberg ('thousand-bucket hill') is the cone-shaped hill at Spitz, so named because it was said to yield a thousand buckets of wine in a good year. It gives fine, perfumed Riesling and Grüner Veltliner.
appellations.terroir: Gneiss and amphibolite terraces wrapping around a steep hill. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Spitz, with about 10 ha delimited.

appellations.terroir: Gneiss and mica schist terraces, south facing. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Spitz, with about 40 ha delimited.

appellations.name: Ried Schön
appellations.summary: A Ried in the Spitzer Graben, the cool side valley behind Spitz where terraces climb to over 500 m. Growers such as Peter Veyder-Malberg, Martin Muthenthaler and Johann Donabaum make lean, ethereal Riesling and Grüner Veltliner here, a different face of the Wachau from the warm river sites.
appellations.terroir: Gneiss and amphibolite terraces in a narrow, cool valley. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Vießling (municipality Spitz), with about 10 ha delimited. Named subrieden: Hölle.

appellations.name: Ried Bruck
appellations.summary: The Bruck in the Spitzer Graben is one of the side valley's best-known Rieden, giving delicate, high-toned Riesling. Several terraces here were rescued from abandonment by a new generation of growers after 2000. Peter Veyder-Malberg came to the Spitzer Graben in 2008 and rescued abandoned terraces that larger estates had given up as uneconomic.
appellations.terroir: Steep gneiss terraces in a cool side valley. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Vießling (municipality Spitz), with about 20 ha delimited. Named subrieden: Stern.

appellations.terroir: Gneiss terraces at altitude. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Elsarn am Jauerling (municipality Mühldorf).

appellations.terroir: Gneiss terraces above 450 m. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Elsarn am Jauerling (municipality Mühldorf), with about 30 ha delimited.

appellations.name: Ried Atzberg
appellations.summary: The Atzberg is a steep terraced hill above Spitz that was abandoned for decades and replanted in the 2000s, a symbol of the effort to save the Wachau's highest terraces.
appellations.terroir: Gneiss terraces rising steeply above the village. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Spitz.

appellations.name: Ried Zornberg
appellations.summary: A Spitz Ried giving fresh, aromatic wines.
appellations.nerd_note: Under Wachau DAC rules (from the 2020 vintage) a Ried name may only appear on hand-harvested wines, while the Vinea Wachau terms Steinfeder, Federspiel and Smaragd still signal rising ripeness.
appellations.terroir: Gneiss and loess. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Spitz, with about 10 ha delimited.

appellations.name: Ried Silberbichl
appellations.summary: The Silberbichl at Mautern is the source of Nikolaihof's Riesling 'Vom Stein', a famously long-lived dry wine. Nikolaihof is often called Austria's oldest wine estate: its buildings stand on the walls of the Roman fort of Favianis, and the estate has farmed biodynamically since 1971. Mautern lies on the south bank opposite Stein, and its vineyards face the Danube from the other side, a cooler, later-ripening exposure.
appellations.terroir: Gneiss and gravel on the south bank of the Danube; the subried Silberbichl Vom Stein is named on the map. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Mautern (municipality Mautern an der Donau), with about 50 ha delimited.
appellations.nerd_note: Nikolaihof ages some Rieslings for many years in old casks before release, the 'Vinothek' bottlings.

appellations.name: Ried Alte Point
appellations.summary: The Alte Point at Mautern includes the subried Im Weingebirge, the source of Nikolaihof's Grüner Veltliner and Riesling 'Im Weingebirge'.
appellations.terroir: Loess and gneiss on the south bank. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Mautern (municipality Mautern an der Donau), with about 30 ha delimited.

appellations.name: Ried Bischofpoint
appellations.summary: A Mautern Ried whose name recalls episcopal ownership; Bavarian bishoprics and abbeys such as Passau, Freising and Tegernsee held much of the Wachau's vineyard land in the Middle Ages.
appellations.terroir: Loess and gneiss. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Baumgarten (municipality Mautern an der Donau), with about 20 ha delimited.

appellations.summary: A Mautern Ried whose name recalls episcopal ownership; Bavarian bishoprics and abbeys such as Passau, Freising and Tegernsee held much of the Wachau's vineyard land in the Middle Ages.

appellations.name: Ried Kirnberg

appellations.terroir: Gneiss and loess. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Rossatz (municipality Rossatz-Arnsdorf), with about 10 ha delimited.

appellations.name: Ried Steiger

appellations.terroir: Gneiss terraces. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Rossatz (municipality Rossatz-Arnsdorf), with about 20 ha delimited. Named subrieden: Himmelreich.

appellations.name: Ried Frauenweingärten

appellations.terroir: Loess and sand. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Rossatz (municipality Rossatz-Arnsdorf), with about 20 ha delimited.

appellations.name: Ried Heiligenstein
appellations.summary: The Heiligenstein is the Kamptal's most famous hill and one of the great Riesling sites of Austria, a south-facing ridge above Zöbing; local tradition holds that its name ('holy stone') is a pious rewriting of an older 'Höllenstein', hell's stone, a nod to its summer heat. It is geologically unique in the region: instead of gneiss or loess, it is built of Permian desert sandstone and conglomerate with volcanic components, about 270 million years old, the so-called Zöbing formation. Its Rieslings are spicy, smoky and long, with a citrus and stone-fruit core and a firm, salty finish. More than a dozen owners share it, led by Bründlmayer, Hirsch, Schloss Gobelsburg, Jurtschitsch, Allram and Hiedler.
appellations.terroir: About 35 ha of terraces between roughly 240 and 350 m. The sandstone weathers into a poor, brittle, stony soil; cool north winds from the Waldviertel ventilate the hill and keep acidity high, while the south face gets intense sun. Subrieden on the official map include Heiligenstein-Rotfels and Heiligenstein-Steinwand. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Zöbing (municipality Langenlois), with about 40 ha delimited.
appellations.nerd_note: Bründlmayer pioneered the open 'lyre' trellis here in the 1980s to spread the canopy and ripen grapes evenly on this exposed hill.

appellations.name: Ried Heiligenstein
appellations.summary: The Kammern end of the Heiligenstein, a small piece of the famous Permian sandstone hill above Zöbing. Its Rieslings share the spicy, salty profile of the main site.
appellations.terroir: Permian sandstone and conglomerate on the eastern flank of the hill. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Kammern (municipality Hadersdorf-Kammern).

appellations.name: Ried Gaisberg
appellations.summary: The Gaisberg is the Heiligenstein's neighbour to the east, but its rock is different: crystalline gneiss, amphibolite and mica schist rather than sandstone. The result is a cooler, more floral and filigree Riesling, with white flowers and citrus, that many tasters prefer for its finesse. Hirsch, Bründlmayer and Schloss Gobelsburg are the leading growers.
appellations.terroir: Terraces of gneiss and mica schist with thin soils, facing south and south-east, rising to over 300 m; the hill spans Zöbing and Kammern. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Zöbing (municipality Langenlois), with about 30 ha delimited.
appellations.nerd_note: Johannes Hirsch, one of the first Austrian estates to move to screwcaps for top wines in 2002, made his name with Gaisberg and Heiligenstein Rieslings.

appellations.name: Ried Gaisberg
appellations.summary: The Kammern side of the Gaisberg, crystalline gneiss and mica schist giving fine, floral Riesling, notably from Hirsch and Schloss Gobelsburg.

appellations.name: Ried Lamm
appellations.summary: The Lamm lies at the south-eastern foot of the Heiligenstein and is planted almost entirely to Grüner Veltliner. Deep loess and loam over the hill's sandstone give opulent, creamy, spicy wines that rank with the most powerful Veltliners of Austria. Schloss Gobelsburg, Bründlmayer, Hirsch and Jurtschitsch bottle it. In warm years Lamm Grüner Veltliner can reach 14 percent alcohol yet stay balanced. Schloss Gobelsburg, leased from the Cistercians of Zwettl abbey by Michael Moosbrugger since 1996, makes one of the most celebrated versions.

appellations.summary: The Käferberg ('beetle hill') rises east of Langenlois, a high site where Bründlmayer and Jurtschitsch make some of the Kamptal's most refined Grüner Veltliner: spicy, deep and long. Langenlois is Austria's largest wine town by vineyard area, and the Käferberg is one of the high, crowning sites on its eastern side, with loess on the lower slope and crystalline rock near the top. Bründlmayer ages its Käferberg in large old oak.
appellations.terroir: Loess and loam over gneiss and amphibolite at around 300 m and above, on south-facing slopes. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Langenlois, with about 40 ha delimited.

appellations.name: Ried Steinmassl

The soils warm slowly in spring, so the site buds and ripens later than the loess slopes below; its Rieslings are among the most delicate of the Kamptal, with white flowers and lime. Fred Loimer farms biodynamically.

Göttlesbrunn's growers turned Carnuntum from a bulk area into a red-wine name in the 1990s; 'Rubin Carnuntum' is the regional label for their Zweigelt.

appellations.nerd_note: Carnuntum is named after the Roman legionary city on the Danube nearby, capital of Pannonia Superior.

It gives Carnuntum's most elegant Blaufränkisch, with a cool, chalky finesse; Dorli Muhr's Muhr-van der Niepoort and Johannes Trapl made it famous after 2000. Dorli Muhr founded the estate with Dirk Niepoort in the early 2000s, returning to her family's home village to revive old vineyards on the hill.

appellations.summary: A Tattendorf Ried on stony gravel in the southern Thermenregion, known for Pinot Noir and St. Laurent from Johanneshof Reinisch.
appellations.terroir: Calcareous gravel of the Steinfeld plain, warm and dry. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Tattendorf, with about 30 ha delimited.

appellations.name: Ried Steingarten
appellations.summary: A Tattendorf Ried of stony gravel giving firm St. Laurent and Pinot Noir.
appellations.nerd_note: The Thermenregion, south of Vienna, is the home of Zierfandler and Rotgipfler on the limestone slopes near Gumpoldskirchen and of Pinot Noir and St. Laurent on the warm gravel plain around Tattendorf.
appellations.terroir: Gravel. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Tattendorf, with about 30 ha delimited.

appellations.name: Ried Lange Bergweingärten
appellations.summary: A Ried on the hills of Sooß near Baden, giving reds and whites on limestone.
appellations.nerd_note: The Thermenregion, south of Vienna, is the home of Zierfandler and Rotgipfler on the limestone slopes near Gumpoldskirchen and of Pinot Noir and St. Laurent on the warm gravel plain around Tattendorf.
appellations.terroir: Limestone and gravel. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Sooß.

appellations.name: Ried Lindenberg
appellations.summary: A large Bad Vöslau Ried with many named subrieden, giving red and white wines; Vöslau was a historic red-wine town.
appellations.terroir: Limestone and gravel on the slopes of the Vienna Woods. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Großau (municipality Bad Vöslau), with about 30 ha delimited. Named subrieden: Heiliger Berg, Predler, Rauhe Bühel, Sonnberg.

appellations.name: Ried Lindenberg
appellations.summary: A large Bad Vöslau Ried with many named subrieden, giving red and white wines; Vöslau was a historic red-wine town.
appellations.terroir: Limestone and gravel on the slopes of the Vienna Woods. The official Lower Austrian Ried map places it in the cadastral village of Gainfarn (municipality Bad Vöslau), with about 10 ha delimited. Named subrieden: Burgstall, Edelmann, Flascheln, Gainfarner Gasse, Kugler, Lange Äcker.

appellations.name: Ried Jungenberg
appellations.summary: A Jois Ried on the northern Leitha hills where Rudolf and Verena Kiss make fine, cool Blaufränkisch, part of a new wave of Leithaberg growers.
appellations.terroir: Schist and limestone on south-facing slopes above Lake Neusiedl. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Jois, with about 40 ha delimited.
appellations.nerd_note: Leithaberg DAC is reserved for Blaufränkisch-based reds and whites from Pinot Blanc, Chardonnay, Neuburger and Grüner Veltliner grown on the limestone and schist of the Leitha hills.

appellations.name: Ried Backobel
appellations.summary: A Jois Ried bottled as a single vineyard by Kiss, giving taut, mineral Blaufränkisch.
appellations.nerd_note: Leithaberg DAC is reserved for Blaufränkisch-based reds and for whites from Pinot Blanc, Chardonnay, Neuburger and Grüner Veltliner grown on the limestone and schist of the Leitha hills.
appellations.terroir: Mica schist and limestone. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Jois, with about 10 ha delimited.

appellations.name: Ried Ladisberg
appellations.summary: A Jois Ried on the slopes of the Leitha hills, giving spicy Blaufränkisch and fresh whites.
appellations.nerd_note: Leithaberg DAC is reserved for Blaufränkisch-based reds and for whites from Pinot Blanc, Chardonnay, Neuburger and Grüner Veltliner grown on the limestone and schist of the Leitha hills.
appellations.terroir: Schist and limestone. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Jois, with about 20 ha delimited.

appellations.name: Ried Hackelsberg
appellations.summary: The Hackelsberg at Jois is a dry, rocky hill and nature reserve with steppe flora above the lake; its vines give spicy Blaufränkisch and firm whites.
appellations.terroir: Mica schist and limestone with thin soils. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Jois, with about 30 ha delimited.

appellations.name: Ried Schieferberg
appellations.summary: A Jois Ried named after its slate ('Schiefer'), giving mineral Blaufränkisch.
appellations.nerd_note: Leithaberg DAC is reserved for Blaufränkisch-based reds and for whites from Pinot Blanc, Chardonnay, Neuburger and Grüner Veltliner grown on the limestone and schist of the Leitha hills.
appellations.terroir: Mica schist. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Jois, with about 10 ha delimited.

appellations.name: Ried Tannenberg
appellations.summary: A Jois Ried giving fresh reds and whites.
appellations.nerd_note: Leithaberg DAC is reserved for Blaufränkisch-based reds and for whites from Pinot Blanc, Chardonnay, Neuburger and Grüner Veltliner grown on the limestone and schist of the Leitha hills.
appellations.terroir: Schist and loam. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Jois, with about 30 ha delimited. Named subrieden: Buschenberg, Ruissland.

appellations.name: Ried Goldberg
appellations.summary: A Purbach Ried on the Leitha hills giving firm Blaufränkisch and Pinot Blanc; Purbach is known for its old cellar lane, the Kellergasse.
appellations.terroir: Limestone and schist. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Purbach am Neusiedler See, with about 20 ha delimited.

appellations.name: Ried Edelberg
appellations.summary: A Purbach Ried giving fresh, mineral whites and reds.
appellations.nerd_note: Leithaberg DAC is reserved for Blaufränkisch-based reds and for whites from Pinot Blanc, Chardonnay, Neuburger and Grüner Veltliner grown on the limestone and schist of the Leitha hills.
appellations.terroir: Limestone and schist. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Purbach am Neusiedler See, with about 20 ha delimited.

appellations.name: Ried Thenau
appellations.summary: A large Ried running down from Purbach towards the lake, giving fruity reds and whites.
appellations.nerd_note: Leithaberg DAC is reserved for Blaufränkisch-based reds and for whites from Pinot Blanc, Chardonnay, Neuburger and Grüner Veltliner grown on the limestone and schist of the Leitha hills.
appellations.terroir: Loam and gravel. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Purbach am Neusiedler See, with about 80 ha delimited.

appellations.name: Ried Thenau
appellations.summary: The Breitenbrunn part of the Thenau, giving supple reds and whites near the lake.
appellations.nerd_note: Leithaberg DAC is reserved for Blaufränkisch-based reds and for whites from Pinot Blanc, Chardonnay, Neuburger and Grüner Veltliner grown on the limestone and schist of the Leitha hills.
appellations.terroir: Loam and gravel. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Breitenbrunn am Neusiedler See, with about 70 ha delimited.

appellations.name: Ried Kirchberg
appellations.summary: A Breitenbrunn Ried on the Leitha slopes giving structured Blaufränkisch.
appellations.nerd_note: Leithaberg DAC is reserved for Blaufränkisch-based reds and for whites from Pinot Blanc, Chardonnay, Neuburger and Grüner Veltliner grown on the limestone and schist of the Leitha hills.
appellations.terroir: Limestone and schist. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Breitenbrunn am Neusiedler See, with about 20 ha delimited.

appellations.name: Ried Sandgraben
appellations.summary: A Breitenbrunn Ried on sandy soils near the lake, giving fresh reds and whites.
appellations.nerd_note: Leithaberg DAC is reserved for Blaufränkisch-based reds and for whites from Pinot Blanc, Chardonnay, Neuburger and Grüner Veltliner grown on the limestone and schist of the Leitha hills.
appellations.terroir: Sand and gravel. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Breitenbrunn am Neusiedler See, with about 60 ha delimited.

appellations.name: Ried Föllikberg
appellations.summary: The Föllikberg is a broad hill at Großhöflein on the southern Leithaberg, giving reds and whites on limestone.
appellations.terroir: Leitha limestone and loam. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Großhöflein, with about 280 ha delimited. Named subrieden: Furtäcker, Föllig, Fölliger Wald und Heide, Fünfjochfeld, Heide, Herrschaftsbreite.

appellations.name: Ried Steinzeilen
appellations.summary: The Steinzeilen at Großhöflein gives Kollwentz's Blaufränkisch 'Steinzeiler', one of the most admired reds of Burgenland: dense, spicy and long. The Steinzeiler is aged in small oak and released late; it sits with the estate's Point and Föllikberg sites on the southern slopes of the Leitha hills, overlooking the Wulka basin.
appellations.terroir: Leitha limestone and schist with stony topsoil. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Großhöflein, with about 20 ha delimited.
appellations.nerd_note: Andi Kollwentz's family helped prove from the 1980s that Burgenland could make world-class dry reds and whites.

appellations.name: Ried Point
appellations.summary: A Großhöflein Ried on the Leitha hills giving fine reds and whites, including Kollwentz wines.
appellations.nerd_note: Leithaberg DAC is reserved for Blaufränkisch-based reds and for whites from Pinot Blanc, Chardonnay, Neuburger and Grüner Veltliner grown on the limestone and schist of the Leitha hills.
appellations.terroir: Limestone and loam. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Großhöflein, with about 10 ha delimited.

appellations.name: Ried Dürr
appellations.summary: A Großhöflein Ried on dry, stony ground, giving firm reds.
appellations.nerd_note: Leithaberg DAC is reserved for Blaufränkisch-based reds and for whites from Pinot Blanc, Chardonnay, Neuburger and Grüner Veltliner grown on the limestone and schist of the Leitha hills.
appellations.terroir: Limestone and gravel. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Großhöflein, with about 20 ha delimited.

appellations.name: Ried Tatschler
appellations.summary: The Tatschler is a limestone site on the edge of Eisenstadt where Kollwentz makes a celebrated Chardonnay, rich and taut.
appellations.nerd_note: Leithaberg DAC is reserved for Blaufränkisch-based reds and for whites from Pinot Blanc, Chardonnay, Neuburger and Grüner Veltliner grown on the limestone and schist of the Leitha hills.
appellations.terroir: Leitha limestone and loam. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Eisenstadt, with about 10 ha delimited.

appellations.name: Ried Goldberg
appellations.summary: The Goldberg at Schützen am Gebirge is the top site of Weingut Prieler, a hill of mica schist whose Blaufränkisch is cool, dense and mineral, among the finest in Austria. Georg Prieler now runs the family estate in Schützen.
appellations.terroir: Mica schist with little topsoil on a south-facing slope of the Leitha hills. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Schützen am Gebirge, with about 20 ha delimited. Named subrieden: Obere Goldberg, Untere Goldberg.
appellations.nerd_note: Prieler's Goldberg was one of the first Austrian Blaufränkisch bottlings to show that schist gives a finer, more mineral style than the loam of the plains.

appellations.name: Ried Vogelsang
appellations.summary: A Rust Ried near the lake, giving whites for Ruster Ausbruch and dry wines; lake mists here encourage noble rot in autumn.
appellations.terroir: Sandy loam and limestone near the shore. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Rust, with about 40 ha delimited.
appellations.nerd_note: Rust, the free town on Lake Neusiedl, is famous for Ruster Ausbruch, a botrytised sweet wine that has its own DAC since 2020; the town's grower families bought their royal charter in 1681 with wine and gold.

appellations.name: Ried Gertberg
appellations.summary: A Rust Ried on the slopes above the town, giving reds and whites.
appellations.nerd_note: Leithaberg DAC is reserved for Blaufränkisch-based reds and for whites from Pinot Blanc, Chardonnay, Neuburger and Grüner Veltliner grown on the limestone and schist of the Leitha hills.
appellations.terroir: Limestone and schist. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Rust, with about 10 ha delimited.

appellations.name: Ried Mariental
appellations.summary: The Mariental is the Rust site of Ernst Triebaumer whose 1986 Blaufränkisch Mariental helped launch the modern era of Austrian red wine. It gives dense, structured, long-lived Blaufränkisch. The 1986 scored so highly in tastings that it became the benchmark for oak-aged Blaufränkisch; Triebaumer's sons continue the estate. Rust itself is famous for the storks that nest on its chimneys every spring.
appellations.terroir: Limestone and schist on a warm slope above the lake. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Rust.

appellations.name: Ried Turner
appellations.summary: A Rust Ried giving rich, sweet and dry whites as well as reds.
appellations.nerd_note: Leithaberg DAC is reserved for Blaufränkisch-based reds and for whites from Pinot Blanc, Chardonnay, Neuburger and Grüner Veltliner grown on the limestone and schist of the Leitha hills.
appellations.terroir: Limestone and loam. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Rust, with about 20 ha delimited.

appellations.name: Ried Greiner
appellations.summary: A low Rust Ried close to the reed belt of the lake, a classic source of botrytis for Ruster Ausbruch.
appellations.nerd_note: Leithaberg DAC is reserved for Blaufränkisch-based reds and for whites from Pinot Blanc, Chardonnay, Neuburger and Grüner Veltliner grown on the limestone and schist of the Leitha hills.
appellations.terroir: Sandy loam near the shore. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Rust, with about 20 ha delimited.

appellations.name: Ried Plachen
appellations.summary: A Rust Ried giving reds and sweet whites.
appellations.nerd_note: Leithaberg DAC is reserved for Blaufränkisch-based reds and for whites from Pinot Blanc, Chardonnay, Neuburger and Grüner Veltliner grown on the limestone and schist of the Leitha hills.
appellations.terroir: Limestone and loam. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Rust, with about 10 ha delimited.

appellations.name: Ried Marienthal
appellations.summary: An Oggau Ried near Rust, giving reds and whites; Oggau is the home of the natural-wine producers Gut Oggau.
appellations.nerd_note: Leithaberg DAC is reserved for Blaufränkisch-based reds and for whites from Pinot Blanc, Chardonnay, Neuburger and Grüner Veltliner grown on the limestone and schist of the Leitha hills.
appellations.terroir: Limestone and loam. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Oggau am Neusiedler See, with about 10 ha delimited.

appellations.name: Ried Kirchberg
appellations.summary: A Winden Ried on the northern Leitha hills, giving Blaufränkisch and Chardonnay from schist and limestone.
appellations.nerd_note: Leithaberg DAC is reserved for Blaufränkisch-based reds and for whites from Pinot Blanc, Chardonnay, Neuburger and Grüner Veltliner grown on the limestone and schist of the Leitha hills.
appellations.terroir: Schist and limestone. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Winden am See, with about 130 ha delimited.

appellations.name: Ried Dürrau
appellations.summary: The Dürrau at Horitschon is one of the great Blaufränkisch sites of Mittelburgenland, where Franz Reinhard Weninger makes a dense, iron-tinged wine from old vines, farmed biodynamically. Weninger also farms vineyards across the Hungarian border near Sopron, where the same grape is called Kékfrankos.
appellations.terroir: Heavy, iron-rich loam and clay over gravel, which holds water through dry summers. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Horitschon, with about 110 ha delimited. Named subrieden: Lauspil, Rakitsch, Thurnau.
appellations.nerd_note: Mittelburgenland became one of Austria's first DACs in 2005, dedicated to Blaufränkisch; the Ödenburg, Landsee and Güns hills shelter it on three sides, and locals call it 'Blaufränkischland'.

appellations.name: Ried Hochäcker
appellations.summary: A Horitschon Ried known for Weninger's Blaufränkisch, fresh and spicy, from loam and gravel.
appellations.nerd_note: Mittelburgenland DAC (since 2005) is dedicated to Blaufränkisch, the grape that covers about half of the district's vineyards.
appellations.terroir: Loam over gravel. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Horitschon, with about 190 ha delimited. Named subrieden: Edelgrund, Kapelln, Kirchholz.

appellations.name: Ried Gfanger
appellations.summary: A Horitschon Ried giving juicy, fruity Blaufränkisch.
appellations.nerd_note: Mittelburgenland DAC (since 2005) is dedicated to Blaufränkisch, the grape that covers about half of the district's vineyards.
appellations.terroir: Loam and gravel. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Horitschon, with about 160 ha delimited. Named subrieden: Oberer Gfanger.

appellations.name: Ried Hochberg
appellations.summary: The Hochberg rises above Neckenmarkt to nearly 380 m, a cool, schist-rich slope whose old-vine Blaufränkisch is among the finest of the district; Moric's Neckenmarkt Alte Reben comes from old vines in this village.
appellations.terroir: Mica schist and gneiss with loam, unusual in a district dominated by heavy clay. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Neckenmarkt, with about 200 ha delimited. Named subrieden: Bodigraben, Himmelsthron, Himmelsthron (Burgstall), Hochgrunderitsch, Kohlenberg, Mittergrunderitsch.

appellations.name: Ried Bergleiten
appellations.summary: A Neckenmarkt Ried on the slopes of the hills, giving spicy Blaufränkisch.
appellations.nerd_note: Mittelburgenland DAC (since 2005) is dedicated to Blaufränkisch, the grape that covers about half of the district's vineyards.
appellations.terroir: Schist and loam. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Neckenmarkt, with about 40 ha delimited. Named subrieden: Oberläng, Weißer Weg.

appellations.name: Ried Kart
appellations.summary: A large Ried around Deutschkreutz, the biggest Blaufränkisch village of the district, giving supple, fruity reds; Gesellmann and others are based here.
appellations.terroir: Loam and clay over gravel. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Deutschkreutz, with about 510 ha delimited. Named subrieden: Baumfeld, Hollinger Weg, Kleinteucht, Kogel, Kolnhoferweg, Pallischkreuz.

appellations.name: Ried Weisses Kreuz
appellations.summary: A large Deutschkreutz Ried named after a wayside cross, giving fruity Blaufränkisch.
appellations.nerd_note: Mittelburgenland DAC (since 2005) is dedicated to Blaufränkisch, the grape that covers about half of the district's vineyards.
appellations.terroir: Loam and gravel. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Deutschkreutz, with about 410 ha delimited. Named subrieden: Dornrainäcker, Frauenbrunnäcker, Gartenäcker, Hochacker, Hölzl, Kleinstraßäcker.

appellations.name: Ried Altes Weingebirge
appellations.summary: The Altes Weingebirge ('old vineyard hill') at Lutzmannsburg on the Hungarian border holds some of the oldest Blaufränkisch vines in Austria; Moric's Lutzmannsburg Alte Reben comes from here and helped redefine the variety after 2001. Roland Velich founded Moric in 2001, rejecting the fashion for heavy oak and extraction in search of a Burgundy-like finesse; his old-vine Lutzmannsburg became one of the most influential Austrian reds of the 2000s.
appellations.terroir: Loam and gravel over gneiss and schist on gentle slopes. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Lutzmannsburg, with about 60 ha delimited. Named subrieden: Auleiter, Marktweger, Neusatz, Schwemmer.

appellations.name: Ried Saybritz
appellations.summary: The Saybritz is one of the top Eisenberg sites, a steep slope of green schist above Deutsch Schützen giving spicy, mineral Blaufränkisch.
appellations.terroir: Green schist and iron-rich loam, south-facing, around 300 to 360 m. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Deutsch Schützen-Eisenberg, with about 60 ha delimited.
appellations.nerd_note: The Eisenberg hill rises on the Hungarian border in southern Burgenland; Eisenberg DAC (since 2010) covers Blaufränkisch from green schist and iron-rich loam.

appellations.name: Ried Szapary
appellations.summary: The Szapary is named after the Hungarian noble family that once owned it. Uwe Schiefer made it famous with taut, profound Blaufränkisch from old vines, including the 'Alter Garten' parcel. Uwe Schiefer, a former Vienna sommelier, began farming the Eisenberg in the 1990s and is credited with revealing the hill's potential.
appellations.terroir: Green schist and iron-rich loam high on the Eisenberg. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Deutsch Schützen-Eisenberg, with about 50 ha delimited.
appellations.nerd_note: Eisenberg means 'iron hill', after the iron oxides in its soils.

appellations.name: Ried Ratschen
appellations.summary: A Deutsch Schützen Ried on the Eisenberg giving fresh, spicy Blaufränkisch, for example from Stubits and Wachter-Wiesler.
appellations.nerd_note: Eisenberg DAC (since 2010) covers Blaufränkisch from the green schist and iron-rich loam of southern Burgenland.
appellations.terroir: Schist and loam. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Deutsch Schützen-Eisenberg, with about 50 ha delimited.

appellations.name: Ried Weinberg
appellations.summary: A Deutsch Schützen Ried giving dense Blaufränkisch from iron-rich soils.
appellations.nerd_note: Eisenberg DAC (since 2010) covers Blaufränkisch from the green schist and iron-rich loam of southern Burgenland.
appellations.terroir: Schist and loam. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Deutsch Schützen-Eisenberg, with about 40 ha delimited.

appellations.name: Ried Reihburg
appellations.summary: The Reihburg is a small Eisenberg Ried where Uwe Schiefer makes a fine, perfumed Blaufränkisch.
appellations.nerd_note: Eisenberg DAC (since 2010) covers Blaufränkisch from the green schist and iron-rich loam of southern Burgenland.
appellations.terroir: Green schist and loam. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Deutsch Schützen-Eisenberg, with about 10 ha delimited.

appellations.name: Ried Csaterberg
appellations.summary: The Csaterberg at Kohfidisch is a small hill with old cellar houses and a traditional wine village atmosphere, giving spicy Blaufränkisch.
appellations.terroir: Green schist and loam, around 280 to 350 m. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Kohfidisch, with about 110 ha delimited. Named subrieden: Hoch Csater, Klein Csater.

appellations.name: Ried Salzberg
appellations.summary: The Salzberg at Gols, on the northern shore of Lake Neusiedl, is the source of Gernot and Heike Heinrich's flagship red, a Blaufränkisch-based wine that showed what the Parndorf plateau's slopes can do. The Heinrichs farm biodynamically and belong to Pannobile, a group of Gols growers who promote local varieties and site-driven blends.
appellations.terroir: Gravel, sand and loam on the slope down from the Parndorf plateau; warm Pannonian climate moderated by the lake. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Gols, with about 40 ha delimited.
appellations.nerd_note: Gols is one of Austria's largest wine villages; its growers led the red-wine boom of the 1990s.

appellations.name: Ried Gabarinza
appellations.summary: The Gabarinza at Gols gives Heinrich's long-running red blend of the same name, built on Zweigelt and Blaufränkisch.
appellations.nerd_note: Neusiedlersee DAC (since 2012) is built on Zweigelt for dry reds and on botrytised sweet wines from the lake's mists.
appellations.terroir: Gravel and loam. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Gols, with about 20 ha delimited.

appellations.name: Ried Altenberg
appellations.summary: A Gols Ried on the edge of the Parndorf plateau, giving firm Blaufränkisch and Zweigelt.
appellations.nerd_note: Neusiedlersee DAC (since 2012) is built on Zweigelt for dry reds and on botrytised sweet wines from the lake's mists.
appellations.terroir: Gravel and loam. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Gols, with about 60 ha delimited.

appellations.name: Ried Ungerberg
appellations.summary: A Gols Ried on the slopes towards the lake, giving fruity Zweigelt and St. Laurent.
appellations.nerd_note: Neusiedlersee DAC (since 2012) is built on Zweigelt for dry reds and on botrytised sweet wines from the lake's mists.
appellations.terroir: Sand and gravel. The official Burgenland Ried map places it in the municipality of Gols, with about 50 ha delimited.

appellations.name: Ried Achleiten Himmelreich
appellations.summary: Himmelreich is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Achleiten at Weißenkirchen, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. The Achleiten is the great hill of Weißenkirchen and Joching, a bulging promontory of terraces that rises from the Danube at the downstream end of the village. It is one of the most complex sites of the Wachau, and its Rieslings and Grüner Veltliners combine ripe stone fruit with a smoky, salty, almost flinty minerality that tasters recognise blind.
appellations.terroir: About 22 ha of dry-stone terraces between roughly 200 and 360 m, facing south and south-west.
appellations.nerd_note: Himmelreich ('kingdom of heaven') is the uppermost part of the Achleiten, where gneiss dominates and the wines are at their most taut.

appellations.name: Ried Steinriegl Lichtgartl
appellations.summary: Lichtgartl is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Steinriegl at Weißenkirchen, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. The Steinriegl ('stone ridge') climbs high behind Weißenkirchen, one of the coolest top sites of the village thanks to its altitude and the winds that drop out of the Waldviertel forest at night. Prager and Domäne Wachau make sleek, perfumed Riesling here.
appellations.terroir: Terraces of gneiss and mica schist rising to over 400 m, south-facing; cooler nights than the river-side sites.
appellations.nerd_note: See the Ried Steinriegl profile for the site's history and growers.

appellations.name: Ried Hochrain Ralais
appellations.summary: Ralais is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Hochrain at Wösendorf, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. The Hochrain above Wösendorf gives some of the Wachau's most elegant Grüner Veltliner and Riesling, notably from Rudi Pichler and Franz Hirtzberger. Loess on the lower terraces softens the wines, gneiss above sharpens them.
appellations.terroir: Terraces of gneiss and paragneiss with loess pockets, facing south-east.
appellations.nerd_note: See the Ried Hochrain profile for the site's history and growers.

appellations.name: Ried Pichl Point Pichl
appellations.summary: Pichl is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Pichl Point at Joching, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. A Joching Ried on gentler slopes near the Danube, giving round, spicy Grüner Veltliner.
appellations.terroir: Loess and sand over gneiss.
appellations.nerd_note: See the Ried Pichl Point profile for the site's history and growers.

appellations.name: Ried Seiberberg Hochseiber
appellations.summary: Hochseiber is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Seiberberg at Weißenkirchen, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. The Seiberberg rises high behind Weißenkirchen, a cool site whose Riesling and Grüner Veltliner are taut and perfumed.
appellations.terroir: Gneiss terraces at around 400 m, among the higher Wachau sites.
appellations.nerd_note: See the Ried Seiberberg profile for the site's history and growers.

appellations.name: Ried Gaisberg Bach
appellations.summary: Bach is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Gaisberg at Wösendorf, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. A Wösendorf Ried on steep terraces, giving fine Riesling and Grüner Veltliner (not to be confused with the Kamptal's Gaisberg).
appellations.terroir: Gneiss terraces.
appellations.nerd_note: See the Ried Gaisberg profile for the site's history and growers.

appellations.terroir: Gneiss and amphibolite.
appellations.nerd_note: See the Ried Jochinger Berg profile for the site's history and growers.

appellations.name: Ried Kellerberg Küss den Pfennig
appellations.summary: Küss den Pfennig is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Kellerberg at Dürnstein, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. The Kellerberg is a steep, terraced slope just west of Dürnstein, and the source of some of the most powerful dry Rieslings and Grüner Veltliners of the Wachau. F.X. Pichler's Kellerberg Smaragds, with their mix of opulence, smoke and cool minerality, made the site famous in the 1990s; Knoll and Domäne Wachau also own parcels.
appellations.terroir: About 15 ha of terraces between about 220 and 400 m, with sandy loess over primary rock of gneiss and quartz.
appellations.nerd_note: See the Ried Kellerberg profile for the site's history and growers.

appellations.name: Ried Loibenberg Rauheneck
appellations.summary: Rauheneck is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Loibenberg at Unterloiben, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. The Loibenberg is the great sun-trap of Loiben, a broad, steep amphitheatre of terraces above Unterloiben facing full south. Its wines are ripe, rich and spicy, with Riesling showing apricot and Grüner Veltliner tobacco and pepper.
appellations.terroir: About 40 ha registered, gneiss and paragneiss with loess on the lower parts; subrieden include Süssenberg, Rothenberg, Langen Zung and Rauheneck.

appellations.summary: Hinterskirchl is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Frauenweingarten at Unterloiben, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. The 'ladies' vineyard' at Loiben recalls the convent of Dürnstein; it gives round, fruity Grüner Veltliner and Riesling.

appellations.summary: Lichtensteinerin is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Kaiserberg at Dürnstein, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. A Dürnstein Ried above the town, giving firm Riesling and Grüner Veltliner.
appellations.terroir: Gneiss terraces.
appellations.nerd_note: See the Ried Kaiserberg profile for the site's history and growers.

appellations.name: Ried Schlossberg Burgweingarten
appellations.summary: Burgweingarten is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Schlossberg at Dürnstein, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. The slope below the ruined castle of Dürnstein, where Richard the Lionheart was held prisoner in 1192 and 1193, gives fine, mineral Riesling.
appellations.terroir: Steep gneiss terraces under the castle rock.
appellations.nerd_note: See the Ried Schlossberg profile for the site's history and growers.

appellations.name: Ried Setzberg Landstallen
appellations.summary: Landstallen is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Setzberg at Spitz, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. The Setzberg runs above Spitz towards the Spitzer Graben, a cool site whose wines are taut and floral; the subrieden Landstallen and Vogelsang are named on the official map.
appellations.terroir: Gneiss and mica schist terraces, south facing.
appellations.nerd_note: See the Ried Setzberg profile for the site's history and growers.

appellations.name: Ried Setzberg Vogelsang
appellations.summary: Vogelsang is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Setzberg at Spitz, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. The Setzberg runs above Spitz towards the Spitzer Graben, a cool site whose wines are taut and floral; the subrieden Landstallen and Vogelsang are named on the official map.
appellations.terroir: Gneiss and mica schist terraces, south facing.

appellations.summary: Almenreith is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Offenberg at Spitz, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. A Spitz Ried giving cool, mineral Riesling and Grüner Veltliner.
appellations.terroir: Gneiss terraces.
appellations.nerd_note: See the Ried Offenberg profile for the site's history and growers.

appellations.name: Ried Axpoint Hochrain
appellations.summary: Hochrain is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Axpoint at Spitz, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. The Axpoint at Spitz is known for Franz Hirtzberger's generous, peppery Grüner Veltliner, grown on loess and gneiss.
appellations.terroir: Loess over gneiss on lower terraces.
appellations.nerd_note: See the Ried Axpoint profile for the site's history and growers.

appellations.name: Ried Steinporz Gasselreith
appellations.summary: Gasselreith is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Steinporz at Spitz, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. A Spitz Ried of rocky terraces, giving stony, aromatic Riesling.
appellations.terroir: Gneiss rock with thin soils.
appellations.nerd_note: See the Ried Steinporz profile for the site's history and growers.

appellations.name: Ried Burgberg Schlossgarten
appellations.summary: Schlossgarten is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Burgberg at Spitz, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. The hill around the castle ruin above Spitz, giving fine Riesling and Grüner Veltliner.
appellations.terroir: Gneiss terraces.
appellations.nerd_note: See the Ried Burgberg profile for the site's history and growers.

appellations.name: Ried Schön Hölle
appellations.summary: Hölle is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Schön at Vießling, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. A Ried in the Spitzer Graben, the cool side valley behind Spitz where terraces climb to over 500 m. Growers such as Peter Veyder-Malberg, Martin Muthenthaler and Johann Donabaum make lean, ethereal Riesling and Grüner Veltliner here, a different face of the Wachau from the warm river sites.
appellations.terroir: Gneiss and amphibolite terraces in a narrow, cool valley.
appellations.nerd_note: See the Ried Schön profile for the site's history and growers.

appellations.name: Ried Bruck Stern
appellations.summary: Stern is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Bruck at Vießling, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. The Bruck in the Spitzer Graben is one of the side valley's best-known Rieden, giving delicate, high-toned Riesling. Several terraces here were rescued from abandonment by a new generation of growers after 2000.
appellations.terroir: Steep gneiss terraces in a cool side valley.
appellations.nerd_note: See the Ried Bruck profile for the site's history and growers.

appellations.name: Ried Silberbichl Vom Stein
appellations.summary: Vom Stein is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Silberbichl at Mautern, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. The Silberbichl at Mautern is the source of Nikolaihof's Riesling 'Vom Stein', a famously long-lived dry wine. Nikolaihof is often called Austria's oldest wine estate: its buildings stand on the walls of the Roman fort of Favianis, and the estate has farmed biodynamically since 1971.
appellations.terroir: Gneiss and gravel on the south bank of the Danube; the subried Silberbichl Vom Stein is named on the map.
appellations.nerd_note: This is the source of Nikolaihof's Riesling 'Vom Stein', one of the longest-lived dry whites of Austria.

appellations.name: Ried Alte Point Im Weingebirge
appellations.summary: Im Weingebirge is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Alte Point at Mautern, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. The Alte Point at Mautern includes the subried Im Weingebirge, the source of Nikolaihof's Grüner Veltliner and Riesling 'Im Weingebirge'.
appellations.terroir: Loess and gneiss on the south bank.
appellations.nerd_note: This is the source of Nikolaihof's Grüner Veltliner and Riesling 'Im Weingebirge'.

appellations.name: Ried Bischofpoint Leukuschberg
appellations.summary: Leukuschberg is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Bischofpoint at Mautern, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. A Mautern Ried whose name recalls episcopal ownership; Bavarian bishoprics and abbeys such as Passau, Freising and Tegernsee held much of the Wachau's vineyard land in the Middle Ages.
appellations.terroir: Loess and gneiss.
appellations.nerd_note: See the Ried Bischofpoint profile for the site's history and growers.

appellations.name: Ried Steiger Himmelreich

appellations.terroir: Gneiss terraces.
appellations.nerd_note: See the Ried Steiger profile for the site's history and growers.

appellations.name: Ried Heiligenstein Heiligenstein-Steinwand
appellations.summary: Heiligenstein-Steinwand is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Heiligenstein at Zöbing, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. The Heiligenstein is the Kamptal's most famous hill and one of the great Riesling sites of Austria, a south-facing ridge above Zöbing; local tradition holds that its name ('holy stone') is a pious rewriting of an older 'Höllenstein', hell's stone, a nod to its summer heat.
appellations.terroir: About 35 ha of terraces between roughly 240 and 350 m.
appellations.nerd_note: Steinwand ('stone wall') names the rocky, terraced flank of the hill.
appellations.classification: ÖTW Erste Lage (1ÖTW) (as part of the Ried Heiligenstein)

The Wachtberg rises above the old town of Krems, a terraced site that the Weingut Stadt Krems (owned by the town since the fifteenth century) has made its flagship. The Grüner Veltliner is dense and spicy, the Riesling fine and stony.
appellations.terroir: Gneiss and mica schist terraces with loess pockets, facing south over the Krems valley.

appellations.name: Ried Obere Sandgrube Frechau
appellations.summary: Frechau is a named subdivision (Subried) of the Ried Obere Sandgrube at Krems, mapped separately on the official Lower Austrian Ried map. The Sandgrube ('sand pit') east of Krems is one of Austria's best-known Grüner Veltliner names, thanks to the Winzer Krems cooperative's 'Sandgrube 13'. The loess and sand here give juicy, peppery Veltliner.
appellations.terroir: Loess and sand on gentle slopes; the subried Frechau is named on the map.
appellations.nerd_note: Frechau is a historic parcel name within the famous Kremser Sandgrube loess area.

appellations.name: Ried Hochäcker Felsengarten

The Hochäcker is a high, iron-rich gneiss slope at Senftenberg in the Krems valley, first documented in 1425. Martin Nigl and Proidl make piercing, mineral Riesling here, among the coolest and most precise of the Kremstal.
appellations.terroir: About 14 ha of weathered gneiss up to about 380 m, with the subried Felsengarten.
appellations.nerd_note: Felsengarten ('rock garden') names the stoniest, most rock-strewn part of the Hochäcker.

The Spitzerberg is a limestone hill rising out of the plain at Prellenkirchen, close to the Slovak border.
